notes.statement: Kamitaki et al. (2020) built a reference panel of 2,530 haplotypes from whole-genome sequence data and used it to impute C4A and C4B copy number into 6,748 European-ancestry SLE cases and 11,516 controls. Across the 11 most common C4A/C4B combinations, SLE risk varied 7-fold. Each copy of C4A was protective (OR 0.54), equivalent to 2.3 copies of C4B (OR 0.77).
quotes: Groups of research participants with the eleven most common combinations of C4A and C4B gene copy number exhibited 7-fold variation in their relative risk of SLE
Logistic-regression analysis estimated that the protection afforded by each copy of C4A (OR: 0.54; 95% CI: [0.51, 0.57]) was equivalent to that of 2.3 copies of C4B (OR: 0.77; 95% CI: [0.71,0.82]).

notes.statement: Kamitaki et al. (2020) used an African American SLE cohort (1,494 cases, 5,908 controls), in which C4-B(S) and HLA-DRB1*03:01 show little linkage disequilibrium, to separate their effects. Joint analysis implicated C4A and C4B but not DRB1*03:01. This indicated that the MHC association with SLE long attributed to DRB1*03:01 arises from C4.
quotes: Joint association analysis of C4A, C4B, and DRB1*0301 implicated C4A (p < 10−14) and C4B (p < 10−5) but not DRB1*0301 (p = 0.29) (Extended Data Table 3).
C4-B(S) alleles consistently increased SLE risk regardless of DRB1*03:01 status, whereas DRB1*03:01 had no consistent effect when controlling for C4-B(S) (Fig. 2b).

notes.statement: After accounting for C4, Kamitaki et al. (2020) mapped an additional, more modest MHC effect on SLE that was independent of C4. It was tagged by rs2105898 and rs9271513 and appeared to involve noncoding variation in the HLA class II XL9 region that is associated with expression levels of many HLA class II genes.
quotes: this effect (tagged by rs2105898 and rs9271513) appeared to involve noncoding variation in the HLA class II XL9 region that associates most strongly with expression levels (rather than the coding sequence) of many HLA class II genes

notes.statement: Kamitaki et al. (2020) found that C4 alleles had stronger effects on SLE risk in men than in women (sex-by-C4 interaction p = 0.002). Common C4A/C4B combinations produced 14-fold variation in SLE risk among men versus 6-fold among women. The C4 alleles that protect against SLE are the same ones that increase schizophrenia risk.
quotes: When a sex-by-C4 interaction term was included in association analyses, this term was significant for both SLE (p = 0.002) and schizophrenia (p = 0.0024), with larger C4 effects in men for both disorders.

common combinations of C4A and C4B generated 14-fold variation in risk for SLE, 31-fold variation in risk for Sjögren's syndrome, and 1.7-fold variation in schizophrenia risk among men (versus 6-fold, 15-fold and 1.26-fold variation in risk among women, respectively)

notes.statement: Kamitaki et al. (2020) found that cerebrospinal fluid from adult men contained on average 27% more C4 protein per C4 gene copy and 42% more C3 protein than that from women. In plasma, these sex differences were most pronounced at ages 20 to 50 years. The authors suggested that higher complement levels in men may explain both the stronger C4 allele effects in men and women's greater risk of SLE.
quotes: CSF from adult men contained on average 27% more C4 protein per C4 gene copy than CSF from women (meta-analysis p = 9.9 × 10−6, Fig. 3c).
CSF levels of C3 protein were also on average 42% higher among men than women (meta-analysis p = 7.5 × 10−7, Fig. 3d).

Sex differences in complement protein levels may help to explain the more potent effects of C4 alleles in men, women's greater risk of SLE and Sjögren's syndrome and men's greater vulnerability to schizophrenia.

notes.statement: Kamitaki et al. (2020) proposed that higher C4 levels likely limit exposure of the adaptive immune system to ribonuclear self-antigens at sites of cell injury, because complement speeds the clearance of debris from dead and injured cells. This would pre-empt the development of autoimmunity.
quotes: Because complement facilitates the rapid clearance of debris from dead and injured cells, elevated levels of C4 protein likely attenuate interactions between the adaptive immune system and ribonuclear self-antigens at sites of cell injury, pre-empting the development of autoimmunity.

notes.statement: Farias et al. (2019) used targeted resequencing of 215 candidate genes in Swedish SLE patients and found a rare variant in intron 4 of MEF2D, rs200395694:G>T, associated with SLE (p = 0.014). Twelve of 504 patients and 6 of 839 controls were heterozygous, giving allele frequencies of 0.011 and 0.003. The authors considered MEF2D a peripheral gene for SLE that has a modest association but an apparent functional effect.
quotes: we identified a rare regulatory variant rs200395694:G > T located in intron 4 of the MEF2D gene encoding the myocyte-specific enhancer factor 2D transcription factor and associated with SLE in Swedish cohorts (504 SLE patients and 839 healthy controls, p = 0.014, CI = 1.1-10)
There were in total 12 heterozygotes out of 504 patients and 6 heterozygotes out of 839 controls giving an allele frequency of 0.011 and 0.003, respectively.
MEF2D shows a rather modest association with SLE in our cohort of Swedish patients but apparent functional effect. Therefore, MEF2D could be considered as a peripheral gene for SLE.

notes.statement: Farias et al. (2019) found that the MEF2D rs200395694 risk allele was associated with a triad of Raynaud phenomenon, anti-RNP antibodies and anti-Sm antibodies (p = 0.00037). All 3 carriers among 140 Swedish patients had all three features, compared with 11 patients (8.5%) of the whole cohort.
quotes: Fisher's exact test revealed an association between the genetic variant and a triad of disease manifestations including Raynaud, anti-U1-ribonucleoprotein (anti-RNP), and anti-Smith (anti-Sm) antibodies (p = 0.00037) among the patients.

notes.statement: Farias et al. (2019) found that the region containing rs200395694 behaved as a cell-specific enhancer. In EMSA, the two alleles bound different proteins, and in luciferase reporter assays their effects differed by cell type and stimulation. In minigene assays, the risk allele inhibited splicing of the tissue-specific alpha-2 isoform of MEF2D but did not affect the alpha-1 isoform. The authors speculated that this might reduce expression of alpha-2 target genes such as DNASE1L3.
quotes: The region has properties of an active cell-specific enhancer, differentially affected by the alleles of rs200395694:G > T. In addition, the risk allele exerts an inhibitory effect on the splicing of the alternative tissue-specific isoform
The alternative isoform α2 generated from the minigene with the rare A allele was significantly repressed in all tested cells.

It is tempting to speculate, for example, that direct correlation between the expression of the α2 transcript and DNASE1L3 would result in suppression of DNASE1L3 in monocytes in the risk genotype where the α2 is inhibited.

notes.statement: Bialas et al. (2017) reported behavioral phenotypes and synapse loss in lupus-prone mice. Blocking type I interferon signaling prevented both. Type I IFN stimulated microglia to become reactive and to engulf neuronal and synaptic material in these mice.
quotes: Here we report behavioural phenotypes and synapse loss in lupus-prone mice that are prevented by blocking type I interferon (IFN) signalling.
we show that type I IFN stimulates microglia to become reactive and engulf neuronal and synaptic material in lupus-prone mice.

notes.statement: Bialas et al. (2017) observed increased type I IFN signaling in post-mortem hippocampal brain sections from patients with SLE. They suggested that synapse loss driven by IFN and dependent on microglia may explain the neurologic symptoms seen in some patients with SLE (CNS lupus). They also suggested this may inform the evaluation of the type I IFN-receptor antagonist anifrolumab.
quotes: our observation of increased type I IFN signalling in post-mortem hippocampal brain sections from patients with SLE may instruct the evaluation of ongoing clinical trials of anifrolumab, a type I IFN-receptor antagonist.

identification of IFN-driven microglia-dependent synapse loss, along with microglia transcriptome data, connects CNS lupus with other CNS diseases and provides an explanation for the neurological symptoms observed in some patients with SLE.

notes.statement: Bialas et al. (2017) noted that up to 75% of patients with SLE have neuropsychiatric symptoms, ranging from anxiety, depression and cognitive impairment to seizures and, rarely, psychosis. These symptoms usually present at lupus diagnosis or within the first year.
quotes: up to 75% of patients with SLE experience neuropsychiatric symptoms that range from anxiety, depression and cognitive impairment to seizures and, in rare cases, psychosis-collectively this is referred to as central nervous system (CNS) lupus.
CNS lupus typically presents at lupus diagnosis or within the first year

notes.statement: Zhao et al. (2017) genotyped SLE cases and controls with the Immunochip. In Chinese, the strongest association was at rs73366469 in the GTF2IRD1-GTF2I intergenic region on 7q11.23 (P = 3.8 x 10(-29), OR = 2.88). The association was confirmed modestly in European Americans but not seen in African Americans. A non-Immunochip SNP, rs117026326 in intron 9 of GTF2I, showed a stronger association and accounted for the rs73366469 signal.
quotes: In Chinese, the strongest association signal was detected at rs73366469 (minor allele frequency of 28.7% in cases versus 12.6% in controls, P=3.8×10−29, OR=2.88) within the GTF2IRD1-GTF2I intergenic region at 7q11.23
rs117026326, located in intron 9 of GTF2I, exhibited stronger association with SLE (Pmeta Chinese=4.4×10−40, OR=2.94; Pmeta EurAm=1.2×10−4, OR=2.83

notes.statement: Zhao et al. (2017) resequenced NCF1 in 45 Chinese subjects using NCF1-specific PCR. They identified a missense variant, p.Arg90His (rs201802880; g.74779296G>A), as the likely causal SLE susceptibility variant at 7q11.23. The variant was associated with SLE in Asians (meta P = 3.1 x 10(-104), OR = 3.47), European Americans (meta P = 1.9 x 10(-7), OR = 2.61) and African Americans (P = 2.9 x 10(-5), OR = 2.02). Conditioning on p.Arg90His removed the association signals at p.Ser99Gly and in the GTF2IRD1-GTF2I region.
quotes: Here we report a missense variant (g.74779296G>A; p.Arg90His) in NCF1, encoding the p47phox subunit of the phagocyte NADPH oxidase (NOX2), as the putative underlying causal variant
Of the variants, only p.Arg90His was associated with SLE (15.7% versus 8.3%, P=2.9×10−5, OR=2.02, Table 1 and Supplementary Table 5).

notes.statement: Zhao et al. (2017) found that the p.Arg90His risk allele of NCF1 was associated with earlier age at SLE onset in a dose-dependent manner in Korean and European American patients.
quotes: Furthermore, the allele encoding p.Arg90Hiswas dose dependently associated with early age of onset in Korean and European-American patients with SLE (Supplementary Fig.3).

notes.statement: Zhao et al. (2017) found that NCF1 copy number affected SLE risk. Having 1 copy of NCF1 was associated with increased risk in Koreans, Chinese and European Americans (OR = 3.91 in European Americans). Having 3 or more copies was protective in Koreans, Chinese, European Americans and African Americans.
quotes: One copy of NCF1 (5:1 ratio) was associated with increased risk of SLE in Koreans (P=0.032), Chinese (P=0.011) and European Americans (P=5.9×10−4, OR=3.91, Supplementary Table 9).

In contrast, having ≥3 copies of NCF1 (3:3 and 2:4 ratios) was protective against developing SLE in Koreans (P=3.7×10−5), Chinese (P=2.8×10−3, OR=0.28), European Americans (P=0.038, OR=0.85) and African Americans (P=0.018, OR=0.73).

notes.statement: Zhao et al. (2017) also found that NCF1 p.Arg90His was associated with other autoimmune diseases. It was associated with primary Sjogren syndrome in Chinese (OR = 2.45) and European Americans (OR = 2.35), and with seropositive rheumatoid arthritis in Koreans, where the effect was modest (OR = 1.65).
quotes: including primary Sjögren’s syndrome ([MIM 270150]) in Chinese (37.8% versus 18.3%, P=7.2×10−17, OR=2.45) and European Americans (4.8% versus 2.2%, P=9.7×10−4, OR=2.35)
seropositive rheumatoid arthritis ([MIM 180300]) in Koreans (26.6% versus 18.1%, P=2.5×10−8, OR=1.65, Table 1 and Supplementary Table 8) but with a modest effect size.

notes.statement: Zhao et al. (2017) noted that Arg90 of p47phox lies in a phosphoinositide-binding pocket of the PX domain and is needed for membrane translocation and NOX2 activation. Earlier in vitro mutation studies had shown that substituting Arg90 reduces ROS production. The authors therefore suggested that p.Arg90His might confer SLE risk by lowering NOX2-derived ROS levels. However, p.Arg90His was not associated with intracellular ROS levels in neutrophils from controls.
quotes: Arg90 of p47phox, located in a phosphoinositide-binding pocket of the PX domain, has a crucial role in the membrane translocation of cytosolic p47phox and resultant activation of NOX2 for ROS production.
These data suggested that p.Arg90His might confer risk for SLE by reducing NOX2-derived ROS levels.
However, p.Arg90Hiswas not associated with intracellular ROS levels in neutrophils from controls (Supplementary Fig.5), probably because of the impact of mitochondrial ROS.

notes.statement: Zhao et al. (2017) cautioned that studies using short sequence reads, such as the 1000 Genomes Project and ExAC, had not called NCF1 variants correctly. This is because NCF1 shares 98% sequence identity with the pseudogenes NCF1B and NCF1C. The authors recommended NCF1-specific PCR and measurement of the deltaGT/GTGT ratio to rule out interference from the pseudogenes.
quotes: Of note, NCF1 variants have not been correctly called in studies using short sequence reads, such as the 1000 Genomes Project (Supplementary Fig.6) and the Exome Aggregation Consortium, owing to the presence of NCF1B and NCF1C.
probably because NCF1 has 98% sequence identity with the nonfunctional pseudogenes NCF1B and NCF1C at 7q11.23 that are located within large DNA duplications

notes.statement: Talaei et al. (2015) found that the promoter region of the NZB gene encoding the SLAM adapter EAT-2, located within a lupus-associated chromosome 1 interval (88-96 cM), was polymorphic. This polymorphism led to an approximately 70% reduction of EAT-2 in dendritic cells. Silencing EAT-2 in dendritic cells without the polymorphism increased IL-12 production and Th1 differentiation in T cell-dendritic cell cocultures, reproducing the phenotype of congenic mice carrying the NZB c1 70-100 cM interval.
quotes: we show that the promoter region of the NZB gene encoding the SLAM signaling pathway adapter molecule EWS-activated transcript 2 (EAT-2) is polymorphic, which results in an ∼ 70% reduction in EAT-2 in DC.

Silencing of the EAT-2 gene in DC that lacked this polymorphism led to increased production of IL-12 and enhanced differentiation of T cells to a Th1 phenotype in T cell-DC cocultures, reproducing the phenotype observed for DC from congenic mice with the NZB c1 70-100 cM interval.

notes.statement: Talaei et al. (2015) showed that SLAM coengagement in dendritic cells inhibited CD40L-induced IL-12 production and blocked p38 MAPK and JNK activation, and that this block was reversed in dendritic cells carrying the NZB EAT-2 allele. They concluded that EAT-2 negatively regulates cytokine production in dendritic cells downstream of SLAM engagement, and that a genetic polymorphism disturbing this process promotes the development of lupus.
quotes: SLAM coengagement blocked activation of p38 MAPK and JNK signaling pathways in DC, which was reversed in DC with the NZB EAT-2 allele.
We conclude that EAT-2 negatively regulates cytokine production in DC downstream of SLAM engagement and that a genetic polymorphism that disturbs this process promotes the development of lupus.

notes.statement: Kshirsagar et al. (2014) found enhanced Stat3 activity in CD4+CD45RA-Foxp3- and Foxp3(low) effector T cells from children with lupus nephritis. This activity correlated with higher frequencies of IL-17-producing cells in these populations. PBMCs from these children also had significantly higher RORC and IL17 mRNA levels than controls.
quotes: we show that enhanced activity of Stat3 in CD4(+)CD45RA(-)Foxp3(-) and Foxp3(low) effector T cells from children with LN correlates with increased frequencies of IL-17-producing cells within these T cell populations
The levels of retinoic acid-related orphan receptor c and IL-17 mRNA are significantly higher in PBMCs from children with LN than in those from controls.

notes.statement: Kshirsagar et al. (2014) found that mTOR inhibition with rapamycin reduced Stat3 activation in effector T cells and lowered the frequency of IL-17-producing T cells in lupus patients. Complement C5a slightly increased IL-17 expression and activated Akt in anti-CD3-activated lupus effector T cells.
quotes: Mammalian target of rapamycin inhibition by rapamycin reduces both Stat3 activation in effector T cells and the frequency of IL-17-producing T cells in lupus patients.
Complement factor C5a slightly increases the expression of IL-17 and induces activation of Akt in anti-CD3-activated lupus effector T cells.

notes.statement: Kshirsagar et al. (2014) showed that Th17 cells from children with lupus nephritis had high Akt activity and enhanced migratory capacity, and that inhibiting Akt signaling significantly decreased their migration. The authors suggested that modulating Akt activity might suppress Th17 cell trafficking to sites of inflammation.
quotes: Th17 cells from children with LN exhibit high Akt activity and enhanced migratory capacity. Inhibition of the Akt signaling pathway significantly decreases Th17 cell migration.
suggest that therapeutic modulation of the Akt activity may inhibit Th17 cell trafficking to sites of inflammation

notes.statement: Mueller et al. (2013) mapped allelic and paralogous sequence variation across the FCGR2/FCGR3 locus on chromosome 1q23 and identified two highly paralogous 24.5-kb blocks within the FCGR2C/FCGR3B/FCGR2B locus. These blocks define the limits of the regions in which nonallelic homologous recombination leads to FCGR2C/FCGR3B copy-number variation. Reduced FCGR3B copy number is associated with increased SLE risk.
quotes: Reduced FCGR3B copy number is associated with increased risk of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).

This analysis identified two highly paralogous 24.5 kb blocks within the FCGR2C/FCGR3B/FCGR2B locus that are devoid of nonpolymorphic paralogous sequence variations and that define the limits of the genomic regions in which nonallelic homologous recombination leads to FCGR2C/FCGR3B copy-number variation.

notes.statement: Using flow cytometry, immunoblotting, and cDNA sequencing, Mueller et al. (2013) found ectopic FcγRIIb on natural killer cells in individuals with FCGR3B-deleted alleles. They concluded that FCGR3B deletion places the 5-prime regulatory sequences of FCGR2C next to the coding sequence of FCGR2B. This creates a chimeric gene that causes FcγRIIb to accumulate on NK cells, which may explain the SLE risk linked to reduced FCGR3B copy number.
quotes: Functionally, we found by flow cytometry, immunoblotting and cDNA sequencing that individuals with FCGR3B-deleted alleles show ectopic presence of FcγRIIb on natural killer (NK) cells.

We conclude that FCGR3B deletion juxtaposes the 5'-regulatory sequences of FCGR2C with the coding sequence of FCGR2B, creating a chimeric gene that results in an ectopic accumulation of FcγRIIb on NK cells and provides an explanation for SLE risk associated with reduced FCGR3B gene copy number.

notes.statement: Manjarrez-Orduño et al. (2012) sequenced CSK exons and conserved intronic regions in 24 European SLE patients homozygous for CSK haplotype 'B'. They then genotyped 3,769 SLE cases and 3,404 controls of European ancestry from 11 cohorts. The A allele of intronic SNP rs34933034 was associated with SLE (allelic OR 1.32; P = 1.04 x 10(-9)).
quotes: We therefore sequenced the CSK exons and five highly conserved intronic regions in a discovery cohort of 24 SLE-affected subjects of European ethnicity, homozygous for the “B” haplotype (Figure 1e).
we genotyped 3769 SLE cases and 3404 controls of European ancestry derived from eleven cohorts and analyzed the data in three groups
The results provide convincing evidence for an association between SLE and the A allele of the variant rs34933034: allelic O.R. 1.32, p-value 1.04 × 10−9.

notes.statement: Manjarrez-Orduño et al. (2012) found that the rs34933034 A allele occurred almost only on the CSK B haplotype (D-prime = 0.95). In conditional analysis using imputed data, the associations of SNPs tagging the B haplotype (e.g., rs8033381) were explained by rs34933034. They observed no genetic interaction between rs34933034 and PTPN22 R620W (rs2476601).
quotes: Linkage disequilibrium analysis shows that the rs34933034 A allele nearly exclusively exists on the B haplotype (D′ = 0.95)
For example, the rs8033381 marker tagging the common B haplotype shows an association (P-value: 9 × 10−8) that is eliminated after conditioning on rs34933034 (P-value: 0.19), (Figure 1, arrowhead).
Of note, we did not observe evidence of genetic interaction between rs34933034 and rs2476601 (PTPN22, R620W).

notes.statement: Manjarrez-Orduño et al. (2012) found that CSK expression was highest in B cells and decreased as B cells matured from transitional to naive to memory cells. In naive B cells from 29 healthy donors homozygous for the B haplotype, the rs34933034 A allele was associated with higher levels of CSK transcripts.
quotes: As previously reported, CSK expression was highest in B cells (Fig 2b), and was inversely correlated with B cell maturity (n = 5, p = 0.03).

We sorted naïve B cells from 29 healthy donors of either rs3493034 genotype, all of whom were homozygous for the B haplotype. As can be seen in Figure 2c higher levels of CSK transcripts in naïve B cells are significantly associated with the rs3493034 A allele.

notes.statement: In healthy carriers, Manjarrez-Orduño et al. (2012) found that the CSK risk allele was associated with increased inhibitory Tyr508 phosphorylation of Lyn in naive B cells. It was also associated with enhanced calcium mobilization after BCR cross-linking and with higher plasma IgM levels, consistent with enhanced activation of mature B cells.
quotes: naïve B cells from subjects carrying the CSK risk allele exhibit higher Tyr508 phosphorylation of Lyn than non-risk allele carriers
As expected, naïve B cells homozygous for the A allele exhibit enhanced calcium mobilization triggered by BCR cross-linking
healthy subjects who carry the CSK risk allele also have more IgM in plasma (n = 44, Figure 3e), compared to subjects with the non-risk allele, consistent with enhanced activation of mature B cells.

notes.statement: In 27 umbilical cord blood samples, Manjarrez-Orduño et al. (2012) found that newborns homozygous for the CSK risk allele had twice the frequency of transitional B cells, due to an expansion of late transitional cells. They suggested this might reflect an impaired tolerance checkpoint or enhanced positive selection, which would lead to more autoreactive B cells.
quotes: we analyzed B cell subpopulations in 27 samples of umbilical cord blood and found that newborn subjects homozygous for the CSK risk allele have double the frequency of transitional cells (CD38hi, CD10hi) compared to levels observed in the cord blood of non-risk subjects
This might reflect an impairment of a tolerance checkpoint or an enhanced positive selection of late transitional B cells.

notes.statement: Boteva et al. (2012) genotyped 2,207 subjects of northern and southern European ancestry (1,028 SLE cases and 1,179 controls). They measured total C4, C4A, and C4B gene copy numbers and the loss-of-function C4 exon 29 CT indel. Using multiple logistic regression that included HLA-DRB1 and MHC region SNPs, they found that genetically determined partial C4 deficiency was not an independent risk factor for SLE in UK and Spanish populations.
quotes: we genotyped 2,207 subjects of northern and southern European ancestry (1,028 SLE cases and 1,179 controls) for total C4, C4A, and C4B gene copy numbers, and the loss-of-function C4 exon 29 CT indel.
We clearly demonstrate that genetically determined partial C4 deficiency states are not independent risk factors for SLE in UK and Spanish populations.

notes.statement: Boteva et al. (2012) found that the C4A exon 29 CT insertion was not associated with SLE in either the UK or the Spanish cohort. They concluded that complete homozygous C4 deficiency is a strong genetic risk factor for SLE, but partial C4 deficiency states do not independently predispose to the disease.
quotes: These results are further corroborated by the lack of association shown by the C4A exon 29 CT insertion in either cohort.
Thus, although complete homozygous deficiency of complement C4 is one of the strongest genetic risk factors for SLE, partial C4 deficiency states do not independently predispose to the disease.

notes.statement: Olsson et al. (2012) found that patients with rheumatoid arthritis were less likely than controls to have an increased copy number of NCF1 (7.6% vs 11.6%; p = 0.037). They suggested that an increased NCF1 copy number may protect against developing RA. They also showed that the T allele of NCF1-339 (rs13447) is expressed in NCF1 and significantly reduces reactive oxygen species production.
quotes: We find that RA patients are less likely to have an increased copy number of NCF1, 7.6%, compared with 11.6% in controls; p=0.037.
We also show that the T-allele of NCF1-339 (rs13447) is expressed in NCF1 and significantly reduces reactive oxygen species production.

notes.statement: Niederer et al. (2010) used a triple paralogue ratio test to measure FCGR3B copy number. In combined UK and Swedish Caucasian SLE cohorts, they found an association between low FCGR3B copy number (0 or 1 copies) and SLE (OR 1.57, 95% CI 1.08-2.27; P = 0.018). They replicated the association in Hong Kong Chinese (OR 1.65, 95% CI 1.25-2.18; P = 4 x 10(-4)), where it was strongest in patients with lupus nephritis.
quotes: combined as a single cohort by meta-analysis (Fig. 3B) showed significant association of low CN with SLE [odds ratio (OR) 1.57, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.08–2.27; P = 0.018]
found a strong association of low CN with SLE (OR 1.65, 95% CI 1.25–2.18; P = 4 × 10−4) with a similar effect size to that in Caucasians
This association was the strongest in the sub-group of Chinese patients with lupus nephritis

notes.statement: Niederer et al. (2010) found that homozygosity for the FCGR2B 232T allele (I232T, rs1050501) was associated with SLE in 2 new Caucasian cohorts from the UK and Sweden. In a meta-analysis of all Caucasian studies, the association was strong (OR 2.26, 95% CI 1.49-3.41).
quotes: further demonstrating a significant association of FcγRIIB-232T allele homozygosity with SLE risk
When all studies involving Caucasian cohorts were analysed in a meta-analysis, there was a strong association with SLE (OR 2.26, 95% CI 1.49–3.41)

notes.statement: Niederer et al. (2010) found weak to moderate linkage disequilibrium between FCGR3B copy number variation and FCGR2B I232T. However, logistic regression showed that each variant had an independent effect on SLE risk.
quotes: There was weak-to-moderate LD in the Caucasian and Chinese control cohorts, as measured by D′
Overall, this indicated that, despite the presence of LD between the loci, FCGR2B-I232T and FCGR3B CNV have independent effects on the risk of developing SLE.

notes.statement: Niederer et al. (2010) found that FCGR3A copy number did not differ significantly between SLE cases and controls, and FCGR3A V176F was not significantly associated with SLE. FCGR2A 131R homozygosity was more frequent in the SLE cohorts (OR 1.3), but the association was not significant.
quotes: The amount of FCGR3A CNV did not vary significantly between SLE cases and controls
The proportion of FcγRIIA-131R homozygotes was increased in the SLE cohorts, although the association was not significant, perhaps due to relatively small numbers
FcγRIIIA-V176F did not show a significant association with SLE.

notes.statement: Niederer et al. (2010) suggested that the strong association of low FCGR3B copy number with SLE points to a role for neutrophils in protection from SLE. They proposed that reduced FcgammaRIIIB expression could lead to increased immune complex deposition and inflammatory damage.
quotes: The strong association of low CN of FCGR3B with SLE suggests a hitherto un-emphasized role of neutrophils in protection from SLE.
Reduced FcγRIIIB expression could thus lead to increased IC deposition and resulting inflammatory damage and disease.

notes.statement: Niederer et al. (2010) found significant differences in FCGR3B copy number between populations. Low copy number was least common in Caucasians (7.4%), intermediate in Chinese and Vietnamese, and highest in Kenyans. FCGR3B copy number was not associated with severe malaria or bacterial sepsis.
quotes: Low FCGR3B CN (0 or 1 copies) was least common in Caucasians, intermediate in Chinese and Vietnamese populations and highest in the Kenyan population.
In neither of the Kenyan cohorts, nor in a cohort of Vietnamese adults treated for severe malaria, was there any association of CN of FCGR3B

notes.statement: Willcocks et al. (2010) found that a SNP in FCGR2B that abrogates the function of the inhibitory Fc receptor FcgammaRIIb was strongly associated with susceptibility to SLE in both Caucasians and Southeast Asians.
quotes: We show that a SNP in human FCGR2B that abrogates receptor function is strongly associated with susceptibility to SLE in both Caucasians and Southeast Asians.

notes.statement: Willcocks et al. (2010) found that the minor allele of the defunctioning FCGR2B SNP was more common in Southeast Asians and Africans, who come from malaria-endemic areas, than in Caucasians. Homozygosity for the minor allele was associated with substantial protection against severe malaria in an East African population (odds ratio = 0.56; P = 7.1 x 10(-5)). The authors suggested that this protection may contribute to the higher frequency of the SNP, and therefore of SLE, in Africans and Southeast Asians.
quotes: The minor allele of this SNP is more common in Southeast Asians and Africans, populations from areas where malaria is endemic, than in Caucasians.
We show that homozygosity for the minor allele is associated with substantial protection against severe malaria in an East African population (odds ratio = 0.56; P = 7.1 x 10(-5)).
This protective effect against malaria may contribute to the higher frequency of this SNP and hence, SLE in Africans and Southeast Asians.

notes.statement: Myouzen et al. (2010) genotyped 14 tag SNPs in the EGR2 gene region in 3 sets of SLE cohorts. They found peak association with SLE susceptibility for rs10761670, in the 5-prime flanking region of EGR2 (pooled OR = 1.23, 95% CI 1.10-1.37; P = 0.00023). The same SNP was also associated with rheumatoid arthritis (OR = 1.15; P = 0.0019), which suggested that EGR2 is a risk factor shared by SLE and RA.
quotes: We then performed a case-control association study using three sets of SLE cohorts by genotyping 14 tag SNPs in the EGR2 gene region. A peak of association with SLE susceptibility was observed for rs10761670 [Pooled: OR = 1.23 (95% CI 1.10-1.37), P=0.00023).
This SNP was also associated with susceptibility to rheumatoid arthritis (RA) [OR = 1.15 (95% CI 1.05-1.26), P = 0.0019), suggesting that EGR2 is a common risk factor for SLE and RA.

notes.statement: Myouzen et al. (2010) found that rs10761670 genotype was positively correlated with EGR2 expression (R = 0.23, P = 0.00072). Two SNPs in complete linkage disequilibrium with rs10761670 (rs1412554 and rs1509957) altered transcription factor binding and transcriptional activity in vitro. The authors suggested that these SNPs may be causal regulatory variants and that increased EGR2 expression may contribute to SLE pathogenesis.
quotes: a significant positive correlation with expression was identified in an SNP located at the 5' flanking region of EGR2 (rs10761670, R=0.23, P=0.00072)

two SNPs (rs1412554 and rs1509957) affected the binding of transcription factors and transcriptional activity in vitro, suggesting that they may be candidates of causal regulatory variants in this region
EGR2 is a genetic risk factor for SLE, in which increased gene expression may contribute to SLE pathogenesis

notes.statement: Gateva et al. (2009) selected SNPs from 2,466 regions that showed nominal association with SLE (P < 0.05) in a genome-wide scan. They genotyped these SNPs in an independent sample of 1,963 cases and 4,329 controls from the US and Sweden. They identified 5 new SLE susceptibility loci at genome-wide significance (P < 5 x 10(-8)): TNIP1 (OR = 1.27), PRDM1 (OR = 1.20), JAZF1 (OR = 1.20), UHRF1BP1 (OR = 1.17), and IL10 (OR = 1.19).
quotes: we selected SNPs from 2,466 regions that showed nominal evidence of association to SLE (P < 0.05) in a genome-wide study and genotyped them in an independent sample of 1,963 cases and 4,329 controls
This replication effort identified five new SLE susceptibility loci (P < 5 x 10(-8)): TNIP1 (odds ratio (OR) = 1.27), PRDM1 (OR = 1.20), JAZF1 (OR = 1.20), UHRF1BP1 (OR = 1.17) and IL10 (OR = 1.19).

notes.statement: Gateva et al. (2009) found that rs7708392, an intronic variant in TNIP1 on 5q33.1, was significantly associated with SLE in all 3 cohorts (combined P = 3.8 x 10(-13)). This SLE risk variant was 21 kb from the psoriasis risk variants near TNIP1 and appeared to be a distinct genetic signal (r2 = 0.001).
quotes: A variant (rs7708392) on 5q33.1 that resides within an intron of TNIP1 (encoding TNF-α-induced protein 3 (TNFAIP3)-interacting protein 1) was significantly associated with SLE in all three cohorts and had a combined P = 3.8 × 10−13 (Fig. 2).
the SLE and psoriasis risk variants are separated by 21 kb and appear to have distinct genetic signals (r2 = 0.001)

notes.statement: Gateva et al. (2009) identified an SLE risk variant, rs6568431 (P = 7.12 x 10(-10)), in the intergenic region between PRDM1 and ATG5. This signal appeared to be distinct from the previously reported ATG5 risk allele rs2245214: the 2 variants had r2 < 0.1, and rs2245214 remained significant after conditioning on rs6568431.
quotes: A second confirmed risk variant (rs6568431, P = 7.12 × 10−10) was identified in an intergenic region between PRDM1 (PR domain containing 1, with ZNF domain, also known as BLIMP1) and ATG5 (APG5 autophagy 5-like).
rs2245214 remains significantly associated with SLE (P < 1 × 10−5) after conditional logistic regression incorporating rs6568431 (Fig. 2)

notes.statement: Gateva et al. (2009) identified an SLE risk variant, rs849142 (P = 1.54 x 10(-9)), in the promoter region of JAZF1. The same variant had previously been associated with type 2 diabetes and with height variation.
quotes: The promoter region of JAZF1 (juxtaposed with another zinc finger gene 1) is a third newly confirmed SLE locus (rs849142, P = 1.54 × 10−9). Of note, this same variant was previously associated with risk of type 2 diabetes and with height variation.

notes.statement: Gateva et al. (2009) identified a nonsynonymous allele of UHRF1BP1 (R454Q; rs11755393, P = 2.22 x 10(-8)) as an SLE risk locus. The allele lies in a region of extended linkage disequilibrium that includes SNRPC, which encodes part of an RNA processing complex often targeted by SLE autoantibodies.
quotes: A fourth newly identified SLE risk locus is defined by a nonsynonymous allele (R454Q) of UHRF1BP1 (ICBP90 binding protein 1; rs11755393, P = 2.22 × 10−8).

The UHRF1BP1 risk allele is in a region of extended LD that encompasses multiple genes, including SNRPC (small nuclear ribonucleoprotein polypeptide C), which is part of a RNA processing complex often targeted by SLE autoantibodies.

notes.statement: Gateva et al. (2009) identified IL10 as an SLE risk locus (rs3024505, P = 3.95 x 10(-8)). The associated variant was identical to a SNP previously associated with ulcerative colitis and type 1 diabetes, suggesting possible shared pathophysiology in the IL10 pathway.
quotes: The fifth newly identified SLE locus is IL10 (interleukin-10; rs3024505, P = 3.95 × 10−8; Fig. 2).

The variant associated with SLE is identical to a SNP recently identified as contributing to risk of ulcerative colitis and type 1 diabetes, suggesting the possibility of shared pathophysiology in the IL10 pathway across these disorders.

notes.statement: Gateva et al. (2009) tested 25 SNPs from 23 previously reported SLE loci and found further evidence of association for 21 of them. Nine loci reached genome-wide significance in the combined dataset: HLA-DRB1 (DR3), IRF5, TNFAIP3, BLK, STAT4, ITGAM, PTPN22, PHRF1 (KIAA1542), and TNFSF4. No association was observed for LYN, SCUBE1, TLR5, or LY9.
quotes: We found further evidence of association for 21 of the variants (P < 0.05), including 9 loci that reached genome-wide significance (P < 5 × 10−8) in the current combined dataset.
Among the loci with genome-wide significant results were HLA-DRB1 (HLA*DR3 or DRB1*0301), IRF5, TNFAIP3, BLK, STAT4, ITGAM, PTPN22, PHRF1 (also called KIAA1542) and TNFSF4 (also called OX40L).
For four previously implicated variants (LYN, SCUBE1, TLR5 and LY9), no evidence of association was observed in the combined dataset.

notes.statement: At the IRAK1-MECP2 locus on Xq28, Gateva et al. (2009) found that the strongest association was with SNPs near IRAK1, which lies within the linkage disequilibrium region surrounding MECP2. They stated that further work would be needed to determine the causal allele.
quotes: SNPs near IRAK1, a gene critical for Toll-like receptor 7 and 9 signaling and located within the identified region of linkage disequilibrium (LD) surrounding MECP2, showed the strongest evidence of association
further work will be required to determine the causal allele in the IRAK1-MECP2 locus

notes.statement: Gateva et al. (2009) identified 21 additional candidate SLE risk loci with P < 1 x 10(-5), including IRF8, TAOK3 (missense variant rs428073, N47S), LYST, and IL12RB2.
quotes: Using a significance threshold of P < 1 × 10−5 in the combined replication sample, we identified 21 additional SLE candidate risk loci (Table 2 and Supplementary Table 2).
Notable candidate genes in this list include: (i) IRF8 (interferon regulatory factor 8)

notes.statement: Gateva et al. (2009) tested 42 variants from 35 loci previously associated with other autoimmune diseases. Five loci showed suggestive association with SLE: IFIH1 (missense rs1990760, P = 3.3 x 10(-7)), CFB (missense R32Q, rs641153), CLEC16A, IL12B, and SH2B3. The CFB association remained significant after conditioning on HLA DR2 and DR3, and the authors stated that further validation was required.
quotes: We observed a highly significant association to SLE of a missense allele of IFIH1 (rs1990760, P = 3.3 × 10−7) that has previously been associated with type 1 diabetes and Graves’ disease.

We also observed an association of SLE with a missense allele (R32Q) of CFB (complement factor B, rs641153) that resides in the HLA class III region and is a validated risk allele for age-related macular degeneration.
A candidate screen of alleles previously associated with other autoimmune diseases suggested five loci (P < 1 x 10(-3)) that may contribute to SLE: IFIH1, CFB, CLEC16A, IL12B and SH2B3.

notes.statement: Gateva et al. (2009) found no evidence of nonadditive interactions among 26 confirmed SLE risk alleles. HLA-DRB1 (DR3), IRF5, and STAT4 each accounted for more than 1% of the genetic variance, and together the 26 loci explained an estimated 8% of total genetic susceptibility to SLE.
quotes: we observed no evidence for non-additive interactions
HLA-DRB1 (HLA*DR3), IRF5 and STAT4 were each estimated to account for over 1% of the genetic variance, whereas the remaining loci each accounted for less than 1% of the variance.
Together, the 26 SLE risk loci explain an estimated 8% of the total genetic susceptibility to SLE.

notes.statement: Han et al. (2009) performed a genome-wide association study of SLE in a Chinese Han population. They genotyped 1,047 cases and 1,205 controls and replicated 78 SNPs in 2 more cohorts (3,152 cases and 7,050 controls). They found 9 new susceptibility loci: ETS1, IKZF1, RASGRP3, SLC15A4, TNIP1, 7q11.23, 10q11.22, 11q23.3, and 16p11.2 (combined P values from 1.77 x 10(-25) to 2.77 x 10(-8)).
quotes: genotyping 1,047 cases and 1,205 controls using Illumina Human610-Quad BeadChips and replicating 78 SNPs in two additional cohorts (3,152 cases and 7,050 controls)
We identified nine new susceptibility loci (ETS1, IKZF1, RASGRP3, SLC15A4, TNIP1, 7q11.23, 10q11.22, 11q23.3 and 16p11.2; 1.77 x 10(-25) < or = P(combined) < or = 2.77 x 10(-8))

notes.statement: In the Chinese Han population, Han et al. (2009) confirmed association of SLE with previously reported loci, including BLK, IRF5, STAT4, TNFAIP3, TNFSF4, 6q21, and 22q11.21 (combined P values from 5.17 x 10(-42) to 5.18 x 10(-12)).
quotes: confirmed seven previously reported loci (BLK, IRF5, STAT4, TNFAIP3, TNFSF4, 6q21 and 22q11.21; 5.17 x 10(-42) < or = P(combined) < or = 5.18 x 10(-12))

notes.statement: Han et al. (2009) compared their findings with earlier GWAS. The comparison highlighted genetic heterogeneity in SLE susceptibility between Chinese Han and European populations.
quotes: Comparison with previous GWAS findings highlighted the genetic heterogeneity of SLE susceptibility between Chinese Han and European populations.

notes.statement: Sánchez et al. (2009) genotyped 9 IL18 SNPs in Spanish SLE cases and controls. They found an association with the rs360719 C allele, which held up in replication cohorts from Italy and Argentina and in meta-analysis (pooled OR = 1.37, 95% CI 1.21-1.54, combined P = 3.8E-07, corrected P = 1.16E-06).
quotes: The SNP (rs360719) surviving correction for multiple tests was genotyped in two replication cohorts from Italy and Argentina.
a significance with rs360719 C-allele remained across the sets and after the meta-analysis (Pooled OR = 1.37, 95% CI 1.21-1.54, combined P = 3.8E-07, Pc = 1.16E-06)

notes.statement: Sánchez et al. (2009) found that relative IL18 mRNA expression in PBMCs was significantly higher in individuals carrying the rs360719 C risk allele. Electrophoretic mobility shift assay showed that this polymorphism creates a binding site for the transcription factor OCT-1. The authors suggested that the variant may help determine SLE susceptibility and IL18 expression.
quotes: We found a significant increase in the relative expression of IL18 mRNA in individuals carrying the rs360719 C-risk allele; in addition we show that the polymorphism creates a binding site for the transcriptional factor OCT-1.

notes.statement: Sthoeger et al. (2009) found that the mean serum level of the alpha-defensin human neutrophil peptide-1 (HNP-1) in SLE patients was significantly higher than in controls (11.07 vs 0.12 ng/microl). Sixty percent of patients had very high serum levels, and 50% had elevated alpha-defensin gene expression in polymorphonuclear cells. High levels correlated with disease activity but not with neutrophil count.
quotes: the mean alpha-defensin level in the sera of all SLE patients (11.07 +/- 13.92 ng/microl) was significantly higher than that of controls (0.12 +/- 0.07 ng/microl)
Moreover, 60% of patients demonstrated very high serum levels (18.5 +/- 13.36 ng/microl) and 50% showed elevated gene expression in polymorphonuclear cells.
High alpha-defensin levels correlated with disease activity, but not with neutrophil count.

notes.statement: Sthoeger et al. (2009) could not detect human beta-defensin-2 (hBD-2) in SLE sera by ELISA. Its mRNA levels in SLE patients were low and similar to those in controls.
quotes: hBD-2 could not be detected by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and its mRNA levels were low in SLE patients and similar to those found in controls.

notes.statement: Sthoeger et al. (2009) concluded that neutrophil activation and degranulation led to alpha-defensin secretion in SLE patients. Because alpha-defensins are immunomodulatory, they suggested that this secretion may activate the adaptive immune system and lead to a systemic response.
quotes: Thus, activation and degranulation of neutrophils led to alpha-defensin secretion in SLE patients. Given the immunomodulatory role of alpha-defensins, it is possible that their secretion may activate the adaptive immune system leading to a systemic response.

notes.statement: Using genomewide association data from 1,239 SLE cases and 1,629 controls of European ancestry, Musone et al. (2008) identified 3 independent SNPs in the TNFAIP3 region on chromosome 6q associated with SLE. The minor alleles of rs13192841 (OR 0.72, P = 7.9 x 10(-6)) and rs6922466 (OR 0.76, P = 0.00039) were protective, whereas the minor allele of the coding SNP rs2230926 increased risk (OR 1.88, P = 0.0016).
quotes: This shows protective effects of the rs13192841 minor allele with an OR of 0.72 (95% CI = 0.62–0.83, P = 7.9 × 10−6) and the rs6922466 minor allele with an OR of 0.76 (95% CI = 0.65–0.88, P = 0.00039).
In contrast, the minor allele of rs2230926 was associated with an increased risk of SLE with an OR of 1.88 (95% CI = 1.27–2.79, P = 0.0016).
In total, 1,239 SLE cases and 1,629 controls were included in this analysis.

notes.statement: Musone et al. (2008) found that the 3 associated SNPs lay in different linkage disequilibrium blocks (pairwise r2 < 0.01) and remained independent in conditional analysis; stratified analyses indicated that, although some rs2230926 signal might reflect intra-European substructure, a signal remained after controlling for it.
quotes: The final three SNPs are in different LD blocks; each pairwise r2 is <0.01 (Fig. 1).
We conclude that, although some signal from rs2230926 may be due to intra-European population substructure, there is strong evidence that a signal remains even after controlling for substructure.

notes.statement: Musone et al. (2008) found that the A20 protein encoded by the rs2230926 risk allele (Cys127) was comparably stable to the Phe127 protein but modestly, consistently less effective at inhibiting TNF-induced NF-kappa-B activity, suggesting a hypomorphic A20 that may contribute to excessive inflammation and autoimmunity.
quotes: These experiments revealed that the minor Cys127 protein is comparably stable relative to the Phe127 protein. Notably, the Cys127 A20 protein is modestly, but consistently, less effective at inhibiting TNF-induced NF-κB activity when similar amounts of the two proteins are expressed
it is likely that a hypomorphic A20 protein may contribute to multiple facets of excessive inflammation and auto-immunity in humans bearing this polymorphism.

notes.statement: Graham et al. (2008) performed a genome-wide association scan of 311,238 SNPs in 431 unrelated SLE cases and 2,155 controls. Three regions reached genome-wide significance: HLA, IRF5/TNPO3, and a novel locus on chromosome 6q23 within the TNFAIP3 gene.
quotes: we tested association of 311,238 successfully genotyped SNPs in 431 unrelated SLE cases and 2155 controls

Three regions met a pre-specified threshold for genome-wide significance (P<5×10−8): the previously defined HLA, IRF5/TNPO3 regions and a novel SLE locus at chromosome 6q23 within the TNFAIP3 gene (Figure 1A).

notes.statement: Graham et al. (2008) found that SNP rs5029939 in TNFAIP3 was associated with SLE (GWAS P = 2.55 x 10(-8)). The association replicated in 740 independent trios (P = 2.47 x 10(-5)), giving a combined meta-analysis P of 2.89 x 10(-12) and an odds ratio of 2.29.
quotes: found an association between SLE and a variant in TNFAIP3 (rs5029939, meta-analysis P = 2.89 x 10(-12), OR = 2.29)
Association with rs5029939 in TNFAIP3 replicated in the trios (trio P value=2.47×10−5), which together with the GWAS data produced a convincing meta-analysis P value = 2.89 ×10−12 (Table 1).

notes.statement: Graham et al. (2008) found that variants in STAT4 (rs3821236, meta P = 8.49 x 10(-11)) and BLK (rs2618476, meta P = 1.7 x 10(-8)) were associated with SLE in both the GWAS and trio datasets. A variant in ITGAM (rs11150610, meta P = 1.72 x 10(-6)) also showed convincing replication.
quotes: Variants in the region of STAT4 and BLK also demonstrated association with SLE in both the GWAS and trio datasets and together produced meta-analysis P values exceeding genome-wide significance (rs3821236 in STAT4, meta P value=8.49×10−11 and rs2618476 in BLK, meta P value = 1.7×10−8)
a variant in ITGAM also demonstrated strong and convincing evidence for replication (rs11150610, meta P value = 1.72×10−6)

notes.statement: Graham et al. (2008) found that the minor allele of rs6920220, a rheumatoid arthritis risk variant about 185 kb upstream of TNFAIP3, was also associated with SLE (P = 8.92 x 10(-5)). The RA protective variant rs10499194 showed no association (P = 0.72). Haplotype and conditional analyses suggested two independent SLE risk signals in the region: one marked by rs6920220 and one by a haplotype carrying the minor alleles of rs10499197 and rs7749323 that spans TNFAIP3.
quotes: We found the minor allele of rs6920220 that contributes to RA risk was also associated with susceptibility to SLE (P value = 8.92×10−5); however, no evidence for association was seen for the rs10499194 RA protective variant (P value = 0.72)
These results suggest that two independent variants in the region of TNFAIP3 contribute to SLE risk

notes.statement: Graham et al. (2008) concluded that the TNFAIP3 missense SNP rs2230926 (in exon 3) may not be the only putative causal variant: a haplotype carrying its minor allele was not associated with SLE, and its association was fully explained by rs10499197 and rs7749323. They suggested that one or more untyped variants on the risk haplotype are responsible for the association.
quotes: Haplotype 5 carries the minor allele of rs2230926 but is not associated with SLE (Supplementary Figure 3). In addition, the association at rs2230926 can be completely explained by the association at rs10499197 and rs7749323
Taken together these results suggest an untyped variant(s) carried on the haplotype tagged by the minor alleles of rs10499197 and rs7749323 is responsible for this SLE association effect.

notes.statement: Orrú et al. (2009) found that the Q263 variant of the PTPN22 R263Q missense substitution protected against systemic lupus erythematosus.
quotes: the Q263 variant conferred protection against human systemic lupus erythematosus, reinforcing the proposal that inhibition of LYP activity could be beneficial in human autoimmunity

notes.statement: Orrú et al. (2009) found that R263Q, a missense substitution in the catalytic domain of the lymphoid tyrosine phosphatase LYP (encoded by PTPN22), reduced phosphatase activity. High-resolution structural analysis showed the molecular basis for this loss of function. This contrasts with the gain-of-function R620W risk variant.
quotes: another missense substitution (R263Q) within the catalytic domain of LYP leads to reduced phosphatase activity. High-resolution structural analysis revealed the molecular basis for this loss of function.

notes.statement: Willcocks et al. (2008) confirmed that low FCGR3B copy number was associated with SLE in Caucasians: they compared 171 UK Caucasian SLE patients with 176 ethnically matched controls (P = 0.027). They found no such association in a Chinese cohort from Hong Kong (159 cases and 150 controls), including when they analyzed patients with lupus nephritis separately.
quotes: In total, 171 samples from Caucasian patients with SLE were compared with 176 ethnically matched control samples. We found lower CN was significantly associated with SLE in Caucasians (P = 0.027;
but such an association was not seen in a Chinese SLE cohort from Hong Kong, comprising 159 cases and 150 controls

notes.statement: Willcocks et al. (2008) found that FCGR3B copy number correlated with FcgammaRIIIb surface expression, soluble serum FcgammaRIIIb, and neutrophil adherence to and uptake of immune complexes. This held both in a family with FcgammaRIIIb deficiency and in healthy individuals. The authors suggested that low copy number predisposes to SLE by reducing neutrophil trafficking to inflammatory lesions and the clearance of immune complexes.
quotes: As in the index family, there was a clear correlation between CN and neutrophil adherence to immunoglobulin-coated surfaces under flow conditions, with high CN individuals having four times the rate of adherence of those with low FCGR3B CN

Our data would suggest that the mechanism underlying this association is a failure of neutrophil trafficking to inflammatory lesions and reduced ability to ingest immune complexes once there, thereby reducing immune complex clearance and predisposing to SLE.

notes.statement: Willcocks et al. (2008) found that, unlike SLE, ANCA-associated systemic vasculitis was associated with high FCGR3B copy number (P = 10(-8)) in 556 patients from 3 UK cohorts compared with 286 controls. When the 2 diseases were compared directly, SLE patients had a lower mean FCGR3B/CD36 ratio than vasculitis patients (P = 0.0028).
quotes: AASV was associated with high CN when cases from all cohorts were compared with controls (P = 10−8 calculated using a Student's t test stratified by plate of samples;
Patients with SLE showed a significantly lower mean FCGR3B/CD36 ratio than patients with AASV (P = 0.0028; Fig. 5 D).

notes.statement: In a case-control association study using genome-wide gene-based SNPs in a Japanese population, Oishi et al. (2008) found that rs3748079, a SNP in the promoter region of the ITPR3 gene on chromosome 6p21, was significantly associated with SLE in 2 independent Japanese case-control samples (P = 1.78 x 10(-8); odds ratio 1.88, 95% CI 1.51-2.35).
quotes: an SNP (rs3748079) located in a promoter region of the inositol 1,4,5-triphosphate receptor type 3 (ITPR3) gene on chromosome 6p21 was significantly associated with SLE in two independent Japanese case-control samples [P=0.0000000178 with odds ratio of 1.88, 95% confidence interval (CI) of 1.51-2.35]

notes.statement: Oishi et al. (2008) found that the ITPR3 rs3748079 SNP was also associated with rheumatoid arthritis (P = 0.0084; OR 1.23) and with Graves disease (P = 0.00036; OR 1.57).
quotes: This particular SNP also revealed associations with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) (P=0.0084 with odds ratio of 1.23, 95% CI of 1.05-1.43) and with Graves' disease (GD) (P=0.00036 with odds ratio of 1.57, 95% CI of 1.22-2.02)

notes.statement: Oishi et al. (2008) found that NKX2.5 bound specifically to the non-susceptible T allele in the region of the ITPR3 promoter that contains rs3748079.
quotes: We found the binding of NKX2.5 specific to the non-susceptible T allele in the region including this SNP.

notes.statement: Oishi et al. (2008) found that a SNP in NKX2.5 was associated with SLE (P = 0.0037; OR 1.74, 95% CI 1.19-2.55). Individuals with the risk genotype at both the ITPR3 and NKX2.5 loci had a higher risk of SLE (OR 5.77). The authors concluded that genetic and functional interactions of ITPR3 and NKX2.5 play a crucial role in the pathogenesis of SLE.
quotes: an SNP in NKX2.5 also revealed an association with SLE (P=0.0037 with odds ratio of 1.74, 95% CI of 1.19-2.55)
Individuals with risk genotype of both ITPR3 and NKX2.5 loci have higher risk for SLE (odds ratio=5.77).

notes.statement: Nath et al. (2008) identified and replicated an association between ITGAM (CD11b) at 16p11.2 and SLE risk in 3,818 individuals of European descent. The strongest association was at the nonsynonymous SNP rs1143679 (P = 1.7 x 10(-17), odds ratio = 1.78).
quotes: We identified and replicated an association between ITGAM (CD11b) at 16p11.2 and risk of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) in 3,818 individuals of European descent.
The strongest association was at a nonsynonymous SNP, rs1143679 (P = 1.7 x 10(-17), odds ratio = 1.78).

notes.statement: Nath et al. (2008) replicated the ITGAM rs1143679 association with SLE in two independent samples of individuals of African descent (P = 0.0002 and 0.003). The overall meta-analysis gave P = 6.9 x 10(-22).
quotes: We further replicated this association in two independent samples of individuals of African descent (P = 0.0002 and 0.003; overall meta-analysis P = 6.9 x 10(-22)).

notes.statement: Nath et al. (2008) concluded that the genetic association between ITGAM and SLE implicates the alpha(M)beta2-integrin adhesion pathway in disease development.
quotes: The genetic association between ITGAM and SLE implicates the alpha(M)beta2-integrin adhesion pathway in disease development.

notes.statement: In a genome-wide scan using 85,042 SNPs, Kozyrev et al. (2008) found an association between SLE and a nonsynonymous SNP in the BANK1 gene (rs10516487, R61H). They replicated the association in 4 independent case-control sets (combined P = 3.7 x 10(-10); OR = 1.38).
quotes: In a genome-wide scan using 85,042 SNPs, we identified an association between SLE and a nonsynonymous substitution (rs10516487, R61H) in the B-cell scaffold protein with ankyrin repeats gene, BANK1.
We replicated the association in four independent case-control sets (combined P = 3.7 x 10(-10); OR = 1.38).

notes.statement: Kozyrev et al. (2008) found 2 BANK1 isoforms: a full-length transcript and an alternatively spliced transcript that lacked exon 2 (Delta2) and encoded a protein without a putative IP3R-binding domain. Expression of the 2 transcripts differed according to a branch point-site SNP, rs17266594, which was in strong linkage disequilibrium with rs10516487. A third associated variant, rs3733197 (A383T), was located in the ankyrin domain.
quotes: We analyzed BANK1 cDNA and found two isoforms, one full-length and the other alternatively spliced and lacking exon 2 (Delta2), encoding a protein without a putative IP3R-binding domain.
The transcripts were differentially expressed depending on a branch point-site SNP, rs17266594, in strong linkage disequilibrium (LD) with rs10516487.
A third associated variant was found in the ankyrin domain (rs3733197, A383T).

notes.statement: Kozyrev et al. (2008) concluded that BANK1 is a susceptibility gene for SLE, with variants affecting regulatory sites and key functional domains. They suggested that the disease-associated variants could contribute to sustained B cell-receptor signaling and to the B-cell hyperactivity characteristic of the disease.
quotes: Our findings implicate BANK1 as a susceptibility gene for SLE, with variants affecting regulatory sites and key functional domains.
The disease-associated variants could contribute to sustained B cell-receptor signaling and B-cell hyperactivity characteristic of this disease.

notes.statement: International Consortium for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Genetics (SLEGEN) et al. (2008) ran a genome-wide association scan with 317,501 SNPs in 720 women of European ancestry with SLE and 2,337 controls. They replicated the findings in two further sample sets totaling 1,846 affected women and 1,825 controls. Apart from HLA and IRF5, they found replicated association in four regions: 16p11.2 (ITGAM), 11p15.5 (KIAA1542), 3p14.3 (PXK), and 1q25.1 (rs10798269).
quotes: We performed a genome-wide association scan using 317,501 SNPs in 720 women of European ancestry with SLE and in 2,337 controls, and we genotyped consistently associated SNPs in two additional independent sample sets totaling 1,846 affected women and 1,825 controls.

we found evidence of association with replication (1.1 x 10(-7) < P(overall) < 1.6 x 10(-23); odds ratio = 0.82-1.62) in four regions: 16p11.2 (ITGAM), 11p15.5 (KIAA1542), 3p14.3 (PXK) and 1q25.1 (rs10798269).

notes.statement: International Consortium for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Genetics (SLEGEN) et al. (2008) found three SNPs in or near ITGAM on 16p11.2 associated with SLE. The strongest was rs9888739 (overall joint P = 1.61 x 10(-23), OR = 1.62). When combined with an independent study, the joint P was 2.02 x 10(-26) (OR = 1.65) at rs9888739 and 3.7 x 10(-16) (OR = 1.42) at rs1143678.
quotes: Outside the HLA region, we found three SNPs associated with SLE in or very near ITGAM on 16p11.2 (Table 1).

The 7,380 independent samples from women of European ancestry used in the two studies produced a combined joint P = 2.02 × 10−26 and OR = 1.65 (95% confidence interval (CI): 1.45–1.88) at rs9888739 and P = 3.7 × 10−16 and OR = 1.42 (95% CI: 1.27–1.61) at rs1143678.

notes.statement: International Consortium for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Genetics (SLEGEN) et al. (2008) found SNP rs4963128 in KIAA1542 on 11p15.5 associated with SLE (OR = 0.78, P = 3.0 x 10(-10)). This SNP lies 23 kb telomeric to IRF7 and is in strong linkage disequilibrium (r2 = 0.94) with rs709266 in IRF7. They also found rs6445975 in PXK on 3p14.3 associated with SLE (P = 7.1 x 10(-9), OR = 1.25), as was the intergenic SNP rs10798269 on 1q25.1 (OR = 0.82, P = 1.11 x 10(-7)), which lies within the 1q23-q25 SLE linkage interval.
quotes: SNP rs4963128 is in KIAA1542 at 11p15.5 (joint OR = 0.78; P = 3.0 × 10−10)

rs4963128 is 23 kb telomeric to IRF7, a gene that is important in interferon-α production, and had an r2 = 0.94 with rs709266 in IRF7. Second, SNP rs6445975 at position 58345217 in PXK showed strong evidence for association (P = 7.1 × 10−9; OR = 1.25).
Third, rs10798269, which lies outside any recognized gene, was also associated with SLE (Table 1; OR = 0.82 and P = 1.11 × 10−7). Notably, this marker is within the 1q23–q25 SLE linkage interval.

notes.statement: International Consortium for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Genetics (SLEGEN) et al. (2008) found the strongest association in the HLA region at 6p21.3. The most significant SNPs, rs3131379 and rs1270942, reached P < 10(-50), and the effect probably reflects the extended HLA-A1-B8-DR3 haplotype. Logistic regression identified two partially independent effects within the HLA region.
quotes: The most significant association was in the HLA region at 6p21.3.
This probably represents the long-range linkage disequilibrium (LD) related to the extended HLA-A1-B8-DR3 haplotype, which is not found to such an extent in non-European populations.
The most significantly associated SNPs achieve P < 10−50 at chromosome 6 positions 31829012 (rs3131379) and 32026839 (rs1270942).

notes.statement: International Consortium for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Genetics (SLEGEN) et al. (2008) confirmed association of SLE with the IRF5/TNPO3 region on 7q32. Their analysis strongly suggested that this association was driven by a haplotype of the previously reported IRF5 SNPs rs752637 and rs729302. They also replicated associations at PTPN22 (rs2476601, P = 5.2 x 10(-6)), FCGR2A (rs1801274, P = 6.78 x 10(-7)), and STAT4 (rs7574865, P = 2.8 x 10(-9)).
quotes: Our analysis strongly suggests that the associations with the IRF5 and TNPO3 region in this study are driven by a haplotype of rs752637 and rs729302 (data not shown).
Our data replicated associations in PTPN22 (ref.), FCGR2A and STAT4 (ref.).

notes.statement: When International Consortium for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Genetics (SLEGEN) et al. (2008) dropped the requirement for replication in all four sample sets, they found additional possible associations in regions containing XKR6, LYN, ATG5, ICA1, BLK, and SCUBE1.
quotes: The associations we identified included markers in genomic regions containing XKR6, LYN, ATG5, ICA1, BLK and SCUBE1 (Table 3).

notes.statement: In stepwise logistic regression, International Consortium for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Genetics (SLEGEN) et al. (2008) found that six SNPs made independent contributions to SLE susceptibility, with a C statistic of 0.67. Together these SNPs explained about 15% of the sibling risk ratio of 29, an estimate the authors described as optimistic. They found no evidence of statistical interaction (epistasis) among the associated SNPs.
quotes: Alternatively considered, the SNPs listed in Table 2 jointly explained ~15% of the sibling risk ratio of 29.
This estimate is optimistic, as it was calculated in the same sample used to select the best SNPs.
Computing all pairwise interactions via logistic regression models did not provide any evidence of a statistical interaction among the associated SNPs, either within or between genes (P > 0.01).

notes.statement: International Consortium for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Genetics (SLEGEN) et al. (2008) described SLE as a multisystem autoimmune inflammatory disease that predominantly affects women (9:1 ratio). They estimated a concordance rate of about 30% in monozygotic twins versus about 3% in dizygotic twins, and a sibling relative risk ratio of 29.
quotes: SLE predominantly affects women (at a 9:1 ratio), particularly during childbearing years, and has strong genetic and environmental components.
The estimated concordance rate among monozygotic twins (~30%) is ten times that among dizygotic twins (~3%), in accordance with a high sibling relative risk ratio (λS = 29).

notes.statement: Hom et al. (2008) genotyped more than 500,000 SNPs in 1,311 SLE cases and 1,783 controls, all North Americans of European descent, plus 1,557 additional public controls. They replicated the top loci in 793 cases and 857 controls from Sweden. Variation upstream of the transcription start sites of BLK and C8orf13 on chromosome 8p23.1 was associated with SLE in both the U.S. and Swedish series (rs13277113; odds ratio, 1.39; P = 1 x 10(-10)).
quotes: We genotyped more than 500,000 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in DNA samples from 1311 case subjects with SLE and 1783 control subjects; all subjects were North Americans of European descent.

Genetic variation in the region upstream from the transcription initiation site of the gene encoding B lymphoid tyrosine kinase (BLK) and C8orf13 (chromosome 8p23.1) was associated with disease risk in both the U.S. and Swedish case-control series (rs13277113; odds ratio, 1.39; P=1x10(-10))

notes.statement: Hom et al. (2008) found that variants on chromosome 16p11.22, near the genes encoding integrin alpha-M (ITGAM, or CD11b) and integrin alpha-X (ITGAX), were associated with SLE in the combined U.S. and Swedish sample (rs11574637; odds ratio, 1.33; P = 3 x 10(-11)).
quotes: variants on chromosome 16p11.22, near the genes encoding integrin alpha M (ITGAM, or CD11b) and integrin alpha X (ITGAX), were associated with SLE in the combined sample (rs11574637; odds ratio, 1.33; P=3x10(-11)).

notes.statement: Hom et al. (2008) found that the SLE-associated promoter-region allele at the C8orf13-BLK locus was associated with altered mRNA levels in B-cell lines, with reduced expression of BLK and increased expression of C8orf13.
quotes: and also with altered levels of messenger RNA in B-cell lines
a promoter-region allele associated with reduced expression of BLK and increased expression of C8orf13

notes.statement: Balada et al. (2008) found that purified CD4+ T cells from 29 SLE patients had significantly lower DNA deoxymethylcytosine content than cells from 30 healthy controls (0.802 vs 0.901, P = 0.007), but transcript levels of DNMT1, DNMT3A, and DNMT3B did not differ between patients and controls.
quotes: SLE patients had a significantly lower CD4(+) T-cell DNA dmC content than controls (0.802 +/- 0.134 versus 0.901 +/- 0.133) (P = 0.007).
No differences in transcript levels were observed for DNMT1, DNMT3A and DNMT3B between patients and controls.

notes.statement: Balada et al. (2008) found that when low complement occurred together with lymphopenia, high anti-dsDNA titers, or a SLEDAI score above 5, at least one of the 3 DNA methyltransferases increased. They suggested that patients with clearly active disease might be responding indirectly to underlying DNA hypomethylation by raising DNMT mRNA levels.
quotes: The simultaneous association of low complement counts with lymphopenia, high titres of anti-double-stranded DNA (anti-dsDNA), or an SLE disease activity index (SLEDAI) of > 5, resulted in the increase of at least one of the three DNA methyltransferases.
It is possible that patients were reacting indirectly to an underlying DNA hypomethylation status by increasing the mRNA levels of DNA methyltransferases when the disease was being definitely active.

notes.statement: Cunninghame Graham et al. (2008) genotyped SNPs across TNFSF4 in 416 UK and 263 Minnesota SLE parent-affected trios and found a single overtransmitted upstream risk haplotype (joint Pu = 1.86 x 10-5, T/U 1.61) and an undertransmitted protective haplotype tagged by the rs844644 A allele. The association was replicated in 424 UK cases versus 642 controls (rs2205960 OR 1.28; rs844644 OR 0.710).
quotes: Haplotype-TDT analysis within the upstream region confirmed that there is a single overtransmitted GCTAATCATTTGA haplotype (4) in both the UK (Pu = 0.0104) and Minnesota datasets (Pu = 3.00 × 10−4; Table 1).

rs2205960 Pu = 7.00 × 10−3, odds ratio (OR) = 1.28, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.07–1.53) and the other of which tags the undertransmitted haplotype (rs844644 Pu = 6.83 × 10−5, OR = 0.710, 95% CI = 0.597–0.840).

notes.statement: Cunninghame Graham et al. (2008) found by conditional logistic analysis that no single genotyped variant accounted for the association in the TNFSF4 upstream region, with the possible exception of rs844644; a recessive model was least favored. Combined P values were 1.91 x 10-6 for rs12039904 and 6.08 x 10-7 for rs844644.
quotes: supports the hypothesis that no single genotyped variant is responsible for the association in the upstream region of TNFSF4

The two variants with the strongest associations were the overtransmitted haplotype-tagging variant, rs12039904 (P = 1.91 × 10−6), and rs844644, which tags the under-transmitted haplotype (P = 6.08 × 10−7).
A recessive model was least favored by the data.

notes.statement: Cunninghame Graham et al. (2008) found no association of SNPs or haplotypes across the receptor gene TNFRSF4 with SLE.
quotes: Transmission-disequilibrium test (TDT) analysis of both individual SNPs and haplotypes across TNFRSF4 showed that none of the SNPs (Pu > 0.05) and none of the haplotypes reached significance (Pu > 0.05; data not shown).

notes.statement: Cunninghame Graham et al. (2008) showed that activated lymphoblastoid cell lines homozygous for the TNFSF4 risk haplotype had more TNFSF4-positive cells and a 6.7-fold increase in TNFSF4 transcript compared with lines homozygous for the protective haplotype, with similar results in peripheral blood lymphocytes from 8 SLE probands. They hypothesized that increased TNFSF4 expression predisposes to SLE by augmenting T cell-APC interaction via TNFRSF4.
quotes: Quantification of TNFSF4 mRNA levels by qRT-PCR showed that the LCL-over cells had a 6.7-fold (P 0.008) increase in the level of TNFSF4 transcript compared to the LCL-under cells (Fig. 2c).
This difference in expression was consistent in eight individuals (P = 0.02; Fig. 2f).

We hypothesize that increased expression of TNFSF4 predisposes to SLE either by quantitatively augmenting T cell-APC interaction or by influencing the functional consequences of T cell activation via TNFRSF4.

notes.statement: Cunninghame Graham et al. (2008) noted that the T allele of rs1234317, which uniquely tags the TNFSF4 risk haplotype, is predicted to destroy a binding site for the transcriptional repressor E4BP4.
quotes: the T allele of rs1234317, which uniquely tags the overtransmitted haplotype, is predicted by the Genomatix SNP analysis web tool to destroy the DNA binding site for the transcriptional repressor E4BP4

notes.statement: Cunninghame Graham et al. (2008) found that TNFSF4 susceptibility variants did not bias the lupus phenotype toward antiphospholipid syndrome, Sjogren syndrome, or lupus nephritis.
quotes: All the two-sample t-tests for all possible SNP-phenotype combinations exceeded 0.2, indicating that the disease susceptibility variants in TNFSF4 did not influence the lupus phenotype toward any of the three subtypes tested.

notes.statement: In a case-control association study of 178 Japanese SLE patients and 899 controls using genome-wide gene-based SNP markers, Kamatani et al. (2008) found a significant association between SLE and rs3130342, an SNP in the 5-prime flanking region of the TNXB gene (P = 9.3 x 10(-7); OR 3.11, 95% CI 1.89-5.28). The association was replicated in an independent set of 203 cases and 294 controls (P = 0.044; OR 1.52).
quotes: An SNP, rs3130342, in a 5' flanking region of the TNXB gene revealed a significant association with SLE [P = 0.000000930, odds ratio (OR) 3.11, with 95% confidence interval (95%CI) of 1.89-5.28] in a Japanese population.
This association was replicated independently with 203 cases and 294 controls (P = 0.0440, OR 1.52, with 95%CI of 1.01-2.78).

notes.statement: Kamatani et al. (2008) found that the association of copy number variation of the adjacent C4 gene with SLE was weaker than that of the TNXB SNP rs3130342 and likely reflected linkage disequilibrium between C4 CNV and this SNP. Stratified analysis showed that the rs3130342 association was independent of the HLA-DRB1*1501 allele. The authors concluded that TNXB is a candidate SLE susceptibility gene in the Japanese population.
quotes: our analysis on this CNV revealed that the association of CNV of the C4 gene was weaker than the SNP in the TNXB gene and likely to reflect the linkage disequilibrium between C4 CNV and this particular SNP.
Stratified analysis also revealed that the association of SNP rs3130342 with SLE was independent of the HLA-DRB1*1501 allele that has been shown to be associated with SLE.

notes.statement: Remmers et al. (2007) found that a SNP haplotype in the third intron of STAT4, marked by rs7574865, was strongly associated with systemic lupus erythematosus in 1,039 patients and 1,248 controls from 3 case series. The haplotype was present on 31% of patient chromosomes vs 22% of control chromosomes (P = 1.87 x 10(-9); odds ratio 1.55).
quotes: in a total of 1039 case patients and 1248 controls from three series of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus

The haplotype marked by rs7574865 was strongly associated with lupus, being present on 31% of chromosomes of case patients and 22% of those of controls (P=1.87x10(-9); odds ratio for having the risk allele in chromosomes of patients vs. those of controls, 1.55).

notes.statement: Remmers et al. (2007) found that, compared with absence of the allele, homozygosity for the STAT4 risk allele was associated with more than double the risk of lupus. They concluded that the same STAT4 haplotype raised the risk of both rheumatoid arthritis and SLE, which suggested a shared pathway for the 2 diseases.
quotes: Homozygosity of the risk allele, as compared with absence of the allele, was associated with a more than doubled risk for lupus and a 60% increased risk for rheumatoid arthritis.
A haplotype of STAT4 is associated with increased risk for both rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus, suggesting a shared pathway for these illnesses.

notes.statement: Remmers et al. (2007) tested SNPs in and around 13 candidate genes in a chromosome 2q region previously linked to rheumatoid arthritis. They then fine-mapped the STAT1-STAT4 region, which identified the STAT4 intron 3 haplotype that they went on to test in lupus case-control series.
quotes: We tested single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in and around 13 candidate genes within the previously linked chromosome 2q region for association with rheumatoid arthritis. We then performed fine mapping of the STAT1-STAT4 region

notes.statement: Lee-Kirsch et al. (2007) identified monoallelic frameshift or missense mutations and one 3-prime UTR variant in the TREX1 gene in 9 of 417 individuals with SLE; none were found in 1,712 controls (P = 4.1 x 10(-7)).
quotes: Here, we report monoallelic frameshift or missense mutations and one 3' UTR variant of TREX1 present in 9/417 individuals with systemic lupus erythematosus but absent in 1,712 controls (P = 4.1 x 10(-7)).

notes.statement: Lee-Kirsch et al. (2007) showed that 2 mutant TREX1 alleles found in SLE patients altered the subcellular targeting of the protein. They concluded that their findings implicated TREX1 in the pathogenesis of SLE.
quotes: We demonstrate that two mutant TREX1 alleles alter subcellular targeting. Our findings implicate TREX1 in the pathogenesis of SLE.

notes.statement: Fanciulli et al. (2007) found a strong association between low FCGR3B copy number and SLE in 536 UK cases compared with UK 1958 birth cohort controls (P = 2.7 x 10(-8)). Individuals with fewer than 2 copies had an increased risk of SLE with nephritis (OR = 2.43) and of SLE without nephritis (OR = 2.21). Among SLE patients, low copy number did not significantly increase the risk of glomerulonephritis.
quotes: When we considered all SLE cases together (n = 536), regardless of renal involvement, the P value of association was 2.7 × 10-8 (95% c.i. = 0 to 2.9 × 10-5).

However, we did not observe any significantly higher risk of acquiring glomerulonephritis in individuals with SLE who possessed fewer than two copies of FCGR3B (OR = 1.09; 95% c.i. = 0.73-1.62, P = 0.660).

notes.statement: Fanciulli et al. (2007) found zero copies of FCGR3B in 25 of 1,279 individuals with autoimmunity (2%), including 21 with SLE, compared with 1 of 862 controls (0.1%). They suggested that complete FCGR3B deficiency confers a very high risk of autoimmunity, particularly SLE.
quotes: We observed zero copies of FCGR3B in 25 out of 1,279 (2%) individuals with autoimmunity (7 SLE patients with glomerulonephritis, 14 with SLE, one with MPA, 1 with Wegener’s granulomatosis and 2 with Graves’ disease) but in only 1 of 862 controls (0.1%).
This suggests that complete FCGR3B deficiency confers a very high risk of autoimmunity, particularly for SLE.

notes.statement: Fanciulli et al. (2007) also found an association between low FCGR3B copy number and Wegener granulomatosis and microscopic polyangiitis. They found no association with the organ-specific autoimmune disorders Graves disease or Addison disease.
quotes: Here we report strong association between FCGR3B copy number and risk of systemic lupus erythematosus (P = 2.7 x 10(-8)), microscopic polyangiitis (P = 2.9 x 10(-4)) and Wegener's granulomatosis in two independent cohorts from the UK (P = 3 x 10(-3)) and France (P = 1.1 x 10(-4)).
We did not observe this association in the organ-specific Graves' disease or Addison's disease.

notes.statement: Fanciulli et al. (2007) noted that FCGR3B, which is expressed on neutrophils, is important in tethering neutrophils to immune complexes and in clearing them. They hypothesized that in SLE, reduced clearance of immune complexes predisposes to disease in the glomeruli and at other sites.
quotes: FCGR3B is expressed by neutrophils and eosinophils and is important in tethering of neutrophils to immune complexes and in clearance of immune complexes. We hypothesize that in individuals with SLE, reduced clearance of immune complexes predisposes to disease in glomeruli and at other sites.
