notes.statement: Yang et al. (2007) studied C4 gene copy-number variation in 1,241 European Americans, including SLE patients, their first-degree relatives and unrelated healthy controls. Compared with controls, patients with SLE had fewer copies of total C4 and of C4A. Having only 2 copies of total C4 significantly raised the risk of SLE (patients 9.3% vs controls 1.5%; OR = 6.514; P = 0.00002), while having 5 or more copies lowered it (5.79% vs 12%; OR = 0.466; P = 0.016).
quotes: In comparison with healthy subjects, patients with SLE clearly had the GCN of total C4 and C4A shifting to the lower side.

The risk of SLE disease susceptibility significantly increased among subjects with only two copies of total C4 (patients 9.3%; unrelated controls 1.5%; odds ratio [OR] = 6.514; P=.00002) but decreased in those with > or =5 copies of C4 (patients 5.79%; controls 12%; OR=0.466; P=.016).

notes.statement: Yang et al. (2007) found that having zero copies (OR = 5.267; P = 0.001) or one copy (OR = 1.613; P = 0.022) of C4A was a risk factor for SLE, whereas having 3 or more copies of C4A appeared to be protective (OR = 0.574; P = 0.012). Family-based association tests suggested that a haplotype with a single short C4B gene, in tight linkage disequilibrium with the TNFA -308A allele, was more likely to be transmitted to patients with SLE.
quotes: Both zero copies (OR=5.267; P=.001) and one copy (OR=1.613; P=.022) of C4A were risk factors for SLE, whereas > or =3 copies of C4A appeared to be protective (OR=0.574; P=.012).

Family-based association tests suggested that a specific haplotype with a single short C4B in tight linkage disequilibrium with the -308A allele of TNFA was more likely to be transmitted to patients with SLE.

notes.statement: Yang et al. (2007) found that among European Americans the gene copy number ranged from 2 to 6 for total C4, 0 to 5 for C4A and 0 to 4 for C4B. Four copies of total C4 and 2 copies each of C4A and C4B were the most common counts, but each accounted for only one-half to three-quarters of the study populations. Long C4 genes correlated with C4A (R = 0.695), and short C4 genes correlated with C4B (R = 0.437).
quotes: The gene copy number (GCN) varied from 2 to 6 for total C4, from 0 to 5 for C4A, and from 0 to 4 for C4B.
Long C4 genes were strongly correlated with C4A (R=0.695; P<.0001). Short C4 genes were correlated with C4B (R=0.437; P<.0001).

notes.statement: In a targeted genome scan of 1q21-43 in 126 lupus multiplex families with 151 affected sib pairs, Wu et al. (2007) found evidence of linkage at 1q32.2 (nonparametric linkage score 2.52, P = 0.006).
quotes: We found evidence of linkage at 1q32.2 in a targeted genome scan of 1q21-43 in 126 lupus multiplex families containing 151 affected sibpairs (nonparametric linkage score 2.52, P = 0.006).

notes.statement: Wu et al. (2007) analyzed 1,416 individuals from 258 Caucasian and 142 Chinese lupus simplex families. They found that a common CR2 haplotype made up of 3 SNPs (rs3813946, rs1048971, rs17615) was associated with lupus susceptibility (P = 0.00001), conferring a 1.54-fold increased risk of disease. They concluded that CR2 is a likely susceptibility gene for human lupus at 1q32.2.
quotes: we analyzed 1,416 individuals from 258 Caucasian and 142 Chinese lupus simplex families and demonstrated that a common three-single-nucleotide polymorphism CR2 haplotype (rs3813946, rs1048971, rs17615) was associated with lupus susceptibility (P = 0.00001) with a 1.54-fold increased risk for the development of disease.
Our findings reveal that CR2 is a likely susceptibility gene for human lupus at 1q32.2

notes.statement: Wu et al. (2007) found that SNP rs3813946, located in the 5-prime untranslated region of CR2, altered transcriptional activity. They suggested this as a potential mechanism by which CR2 could contribute to the development of lupus.
quotes: Single-nucleotide polymorphism 1 (rs3813946), located in the 5' untranslated region of the CR2 gene, altered transcriptional activity, suggesting a potential mechanism by which CR2 could contribute to the development of lupus.

notes.statement: Kowal et al. (2006) found that serum from lupus patients that reacted with both DNA and the NMDA receptor caused cognitive impairment in mice. The mice received the serum intravenously and were given lipopolysaccharide to break down the blood-brain barrier. They showed hippocampal neuron damage and hippocampus-dependent memory impairment.
quotes: serum with reactivity to DNA and NMDAR extracted from lupus patients elicited cognitive impairment in mice receiving the serum intravenously and given lipopolysaccharide to compromise the BBB integrity
Brain histopathology showed hippocampal neuron damage, and behavioral testing revealed hippocampus-dependent memory impairment.

notes.statement: Kowal et al. (2006) eluted IgG from the brain of an SLE patient. The IgG bound DNA and the NMDA receptor and caused neuronal apoptosis when injected into mouse brains. In the brains of 4 more patients with neuropsychiatric lupus, endogenous IgG colocalized with anti-NMDA receptor antibodies. The authors concluded that lupus patients carry circulating anti-NMDA receptor antibodies that can cause neuronal damage and memory deficits if they cross the blood-brain barrier.
quotes: The IgG bound DNA and NMDAR and caused neuronal apoptosis when injected into mouse brains.
We examined four more brains of patients with neuropsychiatric lupus and found that they displayed endogenous IgG colocalizing with anti-NMDAR Abs.
Our results indicate that lupus patients have circulating anti-NMDAR Abs capable of causing neuronal damage and memory deficit, if they breach the BBB, and that the Abs exist within patients' brains.

notes.statement: Graham et al. (2006) replicated association of the IRF5 rs2004640 T allele with SLE in 4 independent case-control cohorts (P = 4.4 x 10(-16)) and by family-based transmission disequilibrium test analysis (P = 0.0006).
quotes: Here we convincingly replicate association of the IFN regulatory factor 5 (IRF5) rs2004640 T allele with SLE in four independent case-control cohorts (P = 4.4 x 10(-16)) and by family-based transmission disequilibrium test analysis (P = 0.0006).

notes.statement: Graham et al. (2006) found that the rs2004640 T allele creates a 5-prime donor splice site in an alternate exon 1 (exon 1B) of IRF5, allowing expression of several unique IRF5 isoforms. They also identified an independent cis-acting variant, linked to the exon 1B splice site, that was associated with elevated IRF5 expression.
quotes: The rs2004640 T allele creates a 5' donor splice site in an alternate exon 1 of IRF5, allowing expression of several unique IRF5 isoforms.
We also identify an independent cis-acting variant associated with elevated expression of IRF5 and linked to the exon 1B splice site.

notes.statement: Graham et al. (2006) found that haplotypes carrying the variant associated with elevated expression but lacking the exon 1B donor site did not confer risk of SLE. They concluded that a common IRF5 haplotype driving elevated expression of multiple unique IRF5 isoforms is an important genetic risk factor for SLE, establishing a causal role for type I IFN pathway genes in human autoimmunity.
quotes: Haplotypes carrying the variant associated with elevated expression and lacking the exon 1B donor site do not confer risk of SLE.

Thus, a common IRF5 haplotype driving elevated expression of multiple unique isoforms of IRF5 is an important genetic risk factor for SLE, establishing a causal role for type I IFN pathway genes in human autoimmunity.

notes.statement: Aitman et al. (2006) found that low copy number of FCGR3B, an ortholog of rat Fcgr3, was associated with glomerulonephritis in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus.
quotes: In humans, low copy number of FCGR3B, an orthologue of rat Fcgr3, was associated with glomerulonephritis in the autoimmune disease systemic lupus erythematosus.

notes.statement: By positional cloning in Wistar Kyoto rats, Aitman et al. (2006) identified loss of the rat-specific Fcgr3 paralog Fcgr3-related sequence (Fcgr3-rs) as a determinant of macrophage overactivity and glomerulonephritis. They concluded that copy number variation of orthologous rat and human Fcgr3 genes is a determinant of susceptibility to immunologically mediated glomerulonephritis.
quotes: Positional cloning identified loss of the newly described, rat-specific Fcgr3 paralogue, Fcgr3-related sequence (Fcgr3-rs), as a determinant of macrophage overactivity and glomerulonephritis in Wistar Kyoto rats.
Here we show that copy number variation of the orthologous rat and human Fcgr3 genes is a determinant of susceptibility to immunologically mediated glomerulonephritis.

notes.statement: In a meta-analysis of 21 studies, Lee et al. (2006) found that the A/A genotype of the TNF-alpha promoter -308 A/G polymorphism was associated with SLE (overall OR, 3.2; 95% CI, 2.0-5.3; P less than 0.001). The overall OR for the risk genotypes (A/A and A/G) was 2.0.
quotes: We have identified 21 studies of this polymorphism and SLE using MEDLINE search.
The overall odds ratio (OR) of the A/A genotype was 3.2 (95% CI=2.0-5.3, P<0.001).
The overall OR for the risk genotypes (A/A and A/G) was 2.0 (CI=1.3-3.1, P<0.001).

notes.statement: Lee et al. (2006) found that when the data were stratified by ethnicity, the TNF-alpha -308 A/A genotype was associated with SLE in European-derived populations (OR, 4.0) but not in Asian-derived populations. The A allele was significantly associated with SLE in Europeans (OR, 2.1) but not in Asian or African populations. The authors concluded that the polymorphism may confer susceptibility to SLE, especially in European-derived populations.
quotes: Stratification by ethnicity indicated that the A/A genotype was associated with SLE in European-derived population (OR=4.0, CI=2.5-6.4, P<0.001). No association was detected in Asian-derived population (OR, 1.3, CI=0.3-6.3, P=0.76).
a significant association was found in European population (OR=2.1, CI=1.6-2.7, P<0.001), but not in Asian (OR=1.4, CI=0.8-2.3, P=0.2) or African (OR=1.2, CI=0.6-2.5, P=0.59) populations.
this meta-analysis demonstrates that the TNF-alpha promoter -308 A/G polymorphism may confer susceptibility to SLE, especially in European-derived population.

notes.statement: Huerta et al. (2006) found that mice immunized with a peptide mimetope of DNA, which produce lupus-like antibodies crossreacting with DNA and the NMDA receptor, lost neurons in the lateral amygdala and developed a behavioral disorder with a deficient response to fear-conditioning paradigms when given epinephrine to open the blood-brain barrier. They concluded that the agent used to open the blood-brain barrier determines which brain region is made vulnerable to neurotoxic antibodies, and that antibodies penetrating brain tissue can alter emotional behavior as well as cognition.
quotes: Here, we show that peptide-immunized mice, given epinephrine to open the BBB, lose neurons in the lateral amygdala and develop a behavioral disorder characterized by a deficient response to fear-conditioning paradigms.

Thus, the agent used to open the BBB determines which brain region is made vulnerable to neurotoxic Abs, and Abs that penetrate brain tissue can cause changes not only in cognitive competence, but also in emotional behavior.

notes.statement: Lee and Nath (2005) carried out a genome search meta-analysis (GSMA) of 12 genome scan results from 9 independent studies, covering 605 families with 1,355 SLE-affected individuals of Caucasian, African American, and Hispanic ethnicity. Two regions, 6p22.3-p21.1 (which contains the HLA region) and 16p12.3-q12.2, reached genome-wide significance.
quotes: Twelve genome scan results generated from nine independent studies have been used for the present GSMA. All together, the data consists of 605 families with 1,355 SLE affected individuals from three self-reported ethnicities; Caucasian, African-American, and Hispanic.
The present study identified two genomic locations at 6p22.3-6p21.1 and 16p12.3-16q12.2 that met genome-wide significance (p<0.000417). The identified region at 6p22.3-6p21.1 contains the HLA region.

notes.statement: Lee and Nath (2005) found 12 other bins with two point-wise p values below 0.05, which they considered highly likely to contain SLE susceptibility loci. These included 2 novel regions, 4q32.1-q34.3 and 13q13.2-q22.2.
quotes: Additionally, there are 12 other bins with two point-wise p-values (Psumrnk and Pord) <0.05, suggesting that these bin regions are highly likely to contain SLE susceptibility loci. Among them, present GSMA also identified two novel regions at 4q32.1-4q34.3 and 13q13.2-13q22.2.

notes.statement: In an analysis restricted to Caucasian populations, Lee and Nath (2005) found the strongest evidence for linkage at 6p21.1-q15 (Psumrnk = 0.00021). They suggested that the novel region at 3q22.1-q25.33 (Psumrnk = 0.01376) may represent an ethnicity-specific SLE linkage.
quotes: However, separate analysis using only Caucasian populations identified the strongest evidence for linkage at chromosome 6p21.1-6q15 (Psumrnk=0.00021). One interesting novel region suggests that 3q22.1-3q25.33 (Psumrnk=0.01376) may be an ethnicity-specific SLE linkage.

notes.statement: In a genome-wide scan of 64 multiplex SLE families with at least one affected male, Xing et al. (2005) found the strongest signal at 13q32 (lod = 3.08) in 18 African American families, using an affected-relative-pair model-free method. Multipoint model-based analysis gave a lod score of 3.13 under a dominant model with a disease allele frequency of 0.0004 and penetrance of 0.5.
quotes: We studied 64 male families by a genome-wide scan for SLE and found the largest signal (lod=3.08) at 13q32 in 18 African American male families using an affected-relative-pair model-free linkage method.

Multipoint model-based linkage analysis generated a lod score of 3.13 in the same chromosomal region with a low-disease allele frequency of 0.0004 and a disease penetrance of 0.5 for the 18 African American male families.

notes.statement: Fine mapping by Xing et al. (2005) in these families and 3 more African American male families placed the SLE predisposing locus in a region tightly linked to marker D13S892. This confirmed the previously reported linkage of SLE to 13q32. The authors suggested that the susceptibility gene in this region is specific to African Americans with a particular form of SLE in which males are at high risk.
quotes: We performed fine mapping in these and three additional African American male families and the SLE predisposing locus was localized to a region tightly linked to the marker D13S892.
suggested that an SLE susceptibility gene in this region is specific to predisposition of African Americans to a specific form of SLE, with males at high risk.

notes.statement: Xing et al. (2005) added 392 individuals from 181 new families to an earlier sample. They replicated the finding that females with SLE who have affected male relatives have a higher prevalence of renal disease than females with SLE who have no affected male relatives. They concluded that multiplex families with an affected male form a distinct subpopulation.
quotes: Previously, our group showed that SLE females with affected male relatives have higher prevalence of renal disease than SLE females with no affected male relatives in a sample of 372 individuals from 159 families.
By adding 392 individuals from 181 new families, we replicated this finding in the largest collection of families with affected males

notes.statement: Xing et al. (2005) found that identity-by-descent (IBD) sharing at 13q32 in African American families with affected males suggested a dominant mode of inheritance.
quotes: Closer examination of IBD sharing at this region suggested a dominant mode of inheritance.

notes.statement: Floto et al. (2005) showed that the SLE-associated FCGR2B polymorphism FcgammaRIIbT(232), which changes a single amino acid in the transmembrane domain, was functionally impaired. The T232 receptor could not inhibit activating receptors because it was excluded from sphingolipid rafts. The authors suggested that the resulting unopposed proinflammatory signaling promotes SLE.
quotes: We show that a recently described SLE-associated polymorphism of FcgammaRIIb (FcgammaRIIbT(232)), encoding a single transmembrane amino acid substitution, is functionally impaired.
FcgammaRIIbT(232) is unable to inhibit activatory receptors because it is excluded from sphingolipid rafts, resulting in the unopposed proinflammatory signaling thought to promote SLE.

notes.statement: Barber et al. (2005) found that treatment of MRL-lpr mice, a model of SLE, with inhibitors of phosphoinositide 3-kinase gamma (PI3Kgamma), a lipid kinase that regulates inflammation, reduced glomerulonephritis and prolonged lifespan. They suggested that PI3Kgamma may be a useful target in the treatment of chronic inflammation.
quotes: Here we examine the use of inhibitors of phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K) gamma, a lipid kinase that regulates inflammation, in the MRL-lpr mouse model of SLE.
Treatment reduced glomerulonephritis and prolonged lifespan, suggesting that P13Kgamma may be a useful target in the treatment of chronic inflammation.

notes.statement: Blank et al. (2005) found that homozygosity for a G-to-C polymorphism at position -343 of the FCGR2B promoter (rs3219018) was associated with SLE in European-Americans (OR = 11.1, P = 0.003).
quotes: Here we report the identification of a polymorphism in the human FCGR2B promoter (dbSNP no. rs3219018) that is associated in homozygosity with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) phenotype in European-Americans (OR=11.1, P=0.003).

notes.statement: Blank et al. (2005) found that the -343C allele lowered transcription from the FCGR2B promoter and reduced binding of the AP1 transcription complex. Activated B cells from -343 C/C SLE patients had significantly less FcgammaRIIb on their surface. The authors suggested that deregulated FCGR2B expression may play a role in the pathogenesis of SLE.
quotes: The G-C substitution correlated with decreased transcription of the FCGR2B promoter, and resulted in decreased binding of the AP1 transcription complex to the mutant promoter sequence.
The surface expression of FcgammaRIIb receptors was significantly reduced in activated B cells from (-343 C/C) SLE patients.
These findings suggest that genetic defects may lead to deregulated expression of the FCGR2B gene in -343 C/C homozygous subjects, and may play a role in the pathogenesis of human SLE.

notes.statement: Lee et al. (2005) performed a meta-analysis of 14 independent studies testing association between CTLA-4 polymorphisms (exon 1 +49, promoter -318 and -1722, and a 3-prime UTR dinucleotide repeat) and SLE. The exon 1 +49 GG genotype was significantly associated with SLE susceptibility (OR = 1.287, 95% CI 1.031-1.562, P = 0.011).
quotes: A total of 14 independent studies (to July 2004) testing association between one or more CTLA-4 polymorphisms and SLE were used in this analysis.
The overall risk, measured by odds ratio (OR), for exon-1 +49 GG genotype is 1.287 [95% confidence interval (CI)=1.031-1.562, P=0.011].

notes.statement: Lee et al. (2005) found on stratification by ethnicity that the CTLA-4 exon 1 +49 GG genotype was associated with SLE in Asians (OR = 1.293, P = 0.026), with a similar but nonsignificant effect in European-derived populations (OR = 1.268, P = 0.230). The G allele was associated with SLE in Asians (OR = 1.246, P = 0.009) but not in Europeans (OR = 0.978, P = 0.780); the authors concluded that the +49 A/G polymorphism influences SLE risk, especially in Asians.
quotes: Stratification by ethnicity indicates the exon-1 +49 GG genotype is associated with SLE, at least in Asians (OR=1.293, 95% CI=1.031-1.620, P=0.026).
The OR for the exon-1 +49 risk allele (G) in Asians is 1.246 (95% CI=1.057-1.469, P=0.009), while Europeans have no evidence of allelic association (OR=0.978, 95% CI=0.833-1.148, P=0.780).
this meta-analysis supports the CTLA-4 exon-1 +49 (A/G) polymorphism influencing the risk for developing SLE, especially in Asians.

notes.statement: McGaha et al. (2005) demonstrated that partial restoration of inhibitory Fc receptor (FcgRIIB) levels on B cells in lupus-prone mouse strains was sufficient to restore tolerance and prevent autoimmunity. FcgRIIB regulated a common B cell checkpoint in genetically diverse lupus-prone strains, and modest changes in its expression could result in either tolerance or autoimmunity.
quotes: we demonstrate that the partial restoration of inhibitory Fc receptor (FcgRIIB) levels on B cells in lupus-prone mouse strains is sufficient to restore tolerance and prevent autoimmunity
FcgRIIB regulates a common B cell checkpoint in genetically diverse lupus-prone mouse strains, and modest changes in its expression can result in either tolerance or autoimmunity.

notes.statement: McGaha et al. (2005) suggested that increasing FcgammaRIIB levels on B cells may be an effective way to treat autoimmune diseases.
quotes: Therefore, increasing FcgammaRIIB levels on B cells may be an effective way to treat autoimmune diseases.

notes.statement: Tao et al. (2005) found that NK T cells from patients with active SLE were highly sensitive to anti-CD95-induced apoptosis compared with those from normal subjects and inactive SLE patients. They also found that CD226 expression was deficient on these cells and that survivin, an antiapoptotic protein, was selectively deficient in freshly isolated NK T cells from active SLE patients.
quotes: NK T cells from active SLE patients are highly sensitive to anti-CD95-induced apoptosis compared with those from normal subjects and inactive SLE patients. CD226 expression is deficient on NK T cells from active SLE patients.
The expression of one antiapoptotic member protein, survivin, is found to be selectively deficient in freshly isolated NK T cells from active SLE patients.

notes.statement: Tao et al. (2005) showed that CD226 preactivation up-regulated survivin and rescued active SLE NK T cells from anti-CD95-induced apoptosis. In transfected COS7 cells, activation of the CD226 pathway inhibited anti-CD95 death signals by stabilizing caspase-8 and caspase-3 and by activating survivin. The authors concluded that deficient CD226 and survivin expression is a molecular basis for the reduced NK T cell number in SLE.
quotes: CD226 preactivation significantly up-regulates survivin expression and activation, which can rescue active SLE NK T cells from anti-CD95-induced apoptosis.
anti-CD95-mediated death signals are inhibited by activation of the CD226 pathway through stabilization of caspase-8 and caspase-3 and through activation of survivin
deficient expression of CD226 and survivin in NK T cells from active SLE is a molecular base of high sensitivity of the cells to anti-CD95-induced apoptosis

notes.statement: Sigurdsson et al. (2005) analyzed 44 SNPs in 13 type I interferon pathway genes in 679 Swedish, Finnish, and Icelandic patients with SLE, 798 unaffected family members, and 438 unrelated controls. SNPs in TYK2 and IRF5 showed strong signals in joint analysis of linkage and association with SLE (unadjusted P less than 10(-7)).
quotes: We analyzed 44 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in 13 genes from the type I IFN pathway in 679 Swedish, Finnish, and Icelandic patients with SLE, in 798 unaffected family members, and in 438 unrelated control individuals for joint linkage and association with SLE.

In two of the genes--the tyrosine kinase 2 (TYK2) and IFN regulatory factor 5 (IRF5) genes--we identified SNPs that displayed strong signals in joint analysis of linkage and association (unadjusted P<10(-7)) with SLE.

notes.statement: Sigurdsson et al. (2005) noted that TYK2 binds the type I IFN receptor complex and IRF5 regulates type I IFN gene expression, and concluded that their findings support an SLE disease mechanism involving key components of the type I interferon system.
quotes: TYK2 binds to the type I IFN receptor complex and IRF5 is a regulator of type I IFN gene expression. Thus, our results support a disease mechanism in SLE that involves key components of the type I IFN system.

notes.statement: Kozlowski et al. (2004) reported 2 brothers from Cape Town with chondrodysplasia punctata (CDP), the younger more severely affected, whose mother had longstanding disseminated lupus erythematosus and epilepsy treated with chloroquine and other agents during both pregnancies. Noting 7 previously reported instances of CDP with maternal lupus erythematosus, the authors concluded that maternal lupus must be regarded as another causative factor in CDP.
quotes: His only sibling, a brother born in 2000 was similarly but more severely affected.

In addition to these affected brothers, seven previous instances of the association of CDP and maternal lupus erythematosus (MLE) have been reported. On this basis, MLE must be regarded as yet another causative factor in CDP.

notes.statement: In a Korean population of 350 SLE patients and 330 controls, Shin et al. (2004) genotyped 6 of 16 DNase I (DNASE1) SNPs and found no significant association with SLE risk. However, the nonsynonymous exon 8 SNP +2373A>G (Gln244Arg) was significantly associated with an increased risk of anti-RNP and anti-dsDNA antibody production among SLE patients. Arg/Arg homozygosity was found in 31.3% of anti-RNP-positive patients versus 14.4% of anti-RNP-negative patients (P = 0.0006, OR = 2.86).
quotes: Genetic associations of polymorphisms in DNase I with the risk of SLE and the production of common autoantibodies were examined in a Korean population (350 SLE patients and 330 controls).
one non-synonymous SNPs in exon 8, +2373A>G(Gln244Arg), was significantly associated with an increased risk of the production of anti-RNP and anti-dsDNA antibodies among SLE patients
The frequency of the homozygous minor allele (Arg/Arg) was much higher in patients who had the anti-RNP antibody (31.3%) than in patients who did not have this antibody (14.4%) (P=0.0006, OR=2.86).

notes.statement: Shin et al. (2004) did not find the DNASE1 exon 2 A/T mutation, previously reported in 2 Japanese SLE patients, in any of 350 Korean SLE patients or 330 Korean controls. Together with earlier reports, they concluded that this finding strongly suggested the mutation is absent in Caucasian, African, and Asian populations.
quotes: the A/T mutation in exon 2 of DNase reported in two Japanese SLE patients was not present in SLE patients (n=350) or controls (n=330) in our Korean population, which combined with the results of previous reports strongly suggests that the mutation is not present in three major ethnic groups

notes.statement: Kyogoku et al. (2004) genotyped 525 North American white SLE patients and 1,961 white controls for the PTPN22 R620W polymorphism. They found that the variant was associated with SLE (genotypic P = 0.00009), with minor (T) allele frequencies of 12.67% in cases and 8.64% in controls.
quotes: The R620W SNP was associated with SLE (genotypic P=.00009), with estimated minor (T) allele frequencies of 12.67% in SLE cases and 8.64% in controls.

notes.statement: Kyogoku et al. (2004) found that one copy of the W620 (T) allele increased SLE risk (OR 1.37; 95% CI 1.07-1.75), and two copies more than doubled this risk (OR 4.37; 95% CI 1.98-9.65). They concluded that PTPN22 plays a fundamental role in regulating the immune system and the development of autoimmunity.
quotes: A single copy of the T allele (W620) increases risk of SLE (odds ratio [OR]=1.37; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.07-1.75), and two copies of the allele more than double this risk (OR=4.37; 95% CI 1.98-9.65).

notes.statement: In a case-control study of 600 Caucasians, Su et al. (2004) found a significant association between the less frequent FCGR2B proximal promoter haplotype and SLE (odds ratio = 1.65; p = 0.0054). The association persisted after adjustment for FCGR2A and FCGR3A polymorphisms (odds ratio = 1.72; p = 0.0083), and the haplotype was not in linkage disequilibrium with them. The authors suggested that an expression variant of FCGR2B is a risk factor for human lupus.
quotes: Our case-control study in 600 Caucasians indicates a significant association of the less frequent FCGR2B promoter haplotype with the SLE phenotype (odds ratio = 1.65; p = 0.0054).

The FCGR2B haplotype has no linkage disequilibrium with previously identified FCGR2A and FCGR3A polymorphisms, and after adjustment for FCGR2A and FCGR3A, FCGR2B showed a persistent association with SLE (odds ratio = 1.72; p = 0.0083).

notes.statement: Su et al. (2004) identified 10 new SNPs in the human FCGR2B promoter and described two functionally distinct proximal promoter haplotypes. In luciferase reporter assays, the less frequent haplotype increased reporter expression in B lymphoid and myeloid cell lines, both constitutively and after stimulation.
quotes: We have identified 10 novel single-nucleotide polymorphisms in the promoter region of human FCGR2B gene and characterized two functionally distinct haplotypes in its proximal promoter.

In luciferase reporter assays, the less frequent promoter haplotype leads to increased expression of the reporter gene in both B lymphoid and myeloid cell lines under constitutive and stimulated conditions.

notes.statement: Barreto et al. (2004) studied two CTLA4 polymorphisms in SLE: a SNP at position +49 of exon 1 and a dinucleotide repeat in the 3-prime UTR. The 3-prime UTR repeat was significantly associated with SLE, with one allele conferring susceptibility and another conferring protection. The +49 exon 1 SNP showed no association in their population.
quotes: The 3'UTR repeat showed a significant association with SLE, with one allele conferring susceptibility and another conferring protection to the disease.
No association of the exon 1 SNP with SLE was found in our population.

notes.statement: Barreto et al. (2004) concluded that the alleles associated with SLE did not support an allele size-dependent effect of the CTLA4 3-prime UTR repeat. Instead, they suggested the repeat is in linkage disequilibrium with a true causative locus.
quotes: The associated alleles do not support previous suggestions of an allele size-dependent effect of the 3' UTR polymorphism in autoimmunity development and instead suggest that it is in linkage disequilibrium with a true causative locus.

notes.statement: Barreto et al. (2004) performed a meta-analysis of seven previously published studies plus their own on the CTLA4 +49 exon 1 SNP. Carriers of the G allele had a significantly increased risk of SLE, and carriers of the A allele had a significantly decreased risk.
quotes: we performed a meta-analysis including seven previously published studies and the present one. Significantly increased and decreased risks for SLE were found for carriers of the G allele and the A allele, respectively.

notes.statement: Tournoy et al. (2004) found that mice with partial presenilin deficiency (PS1+/- PS2-/-) had a normal phenotype until about 6 months of age. After that, most developed an autoimmune disease resembling human systemic lupus erythematosus, with dermatitis, glomerulonephritis, keratitis and vasculitis. The mice also had B-cell-dominated infiltrates, hypergammaglobulinemia with immune complex deposits in several tissues, high-titer nuclear autoantibodies and an increased CD4+/CD8+ ratio.
quotes: Their phenotype is normal up to approximately 6 months, when the majority of the mice develop an autoimmune disease characterized by dermatitis, glomerulonephritis, keratitis and vasculitis, as seen in human systemic lupus erythematosus.
Besides B-cell dominated infiltrates, we observe a hypergammaglobulinemia with immune complex deposits in several tissues, high-titer nuclear autoantibodies and an increased CD4+/CD8+ ratio.

notes.statement: Tournoy et al. (2004) found that PS1+/- PS2-/- mice had lower PS1 protein levels, reduced gamma-secretase activity and impaired downregulation of beta-catenin. PS1+/- PS2+/- mice stayed healthy, which the authors suggested points towards a sharply defined minimum of presenilin function.
quotes: In these 'partial deficient' mice, PS1 protein concentration is considerably lowered, functionally reflected by reduced gamma-secretase activity and impaired beta-catenin downregulation.
As PS1+/-PS2+/- mice remain healthy, this points towards a sharply defined minimum of PS function.

notes.statement: Using gene microarray profiling validated by functional and biochemical studies, Xu et al. (2004) found that activated T cells from SLE patients resisted anergy and apoptosis by markedly upregulating and sustaining COX-2 expression. Inhibiting COX-2 caused apoptosis of these anergy-resistant lupus T cells by augmenting Fas signaling and markedly decreasing the survival molecule c-FLIP.
quotes: we establish here that activated T cells of lupus patients resist anergy and apoptosis by markedly upregulating and sustaining cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) expression
Inhibition of COX-2 caused apoptosis of the anergy-resistant lupus T cells by augmenting Fas signaling and markedly decreasing the survival molecule c-FLIP

notes.statement: Studies by Xu et al. (2004) with COX-2 inhibitors and Cox-2-deficient mice confirmed that the COX-2/FLIP antiapoptosis program was used selectively by anergy-resistant lupus T cells, not by cancer cells or other autoimmune T cells.
quotes: Studies with COX-2 inhibitors and Cox-2-deficient mice confirmed that this COX-2/FLIP antiapoptosis program is used selectively by anergy-resistant lupus T cells, and not by cancer cells or other autoimmune T cells.

notes.statement: Xu et al. (2004) found that only some COX-2 inhibitors could suppress production of pathogenic anti-DNA autoantibodies by causing autoimmune T-cell apoptosis, an effect independent of PGE2. They suggested this could be useful in designing lupus therapies.
quotes: We also found that only some COX-2 inhibitors were able to suppress the production of pathogenic autoantibodies to DNA by causing autoimmune T-cell apoptosis, an effect that was independent of prostaglandin E(2) (PGE(2)).
These findings could be useful in the design of lupus therapies.

notes.statement: Xu et al. (2004) noted that the gene encoding COX-2 is located in a lupus-susceptibility region on chromosome 1.
quotes: Notably, the gene encoding COX-2 is located in a lupus-susceptibility region on chromosome 1.

notes.statement: Li et al. (2004) used genome-wide scans for genes predisposing to aberrant activation of self-reactive CD5+ B1 cells in SLE-prone NZB mice and their F1 cross with NZW mice, and found evidence that Ltk, encoding leukocyte tyrosine kinase, is a possible candidate.
quotes: Our genome-wide scans to search for susceptibility genes for aberrant activation of B1 cells in these mice showed evidence that the gene, Ltk, encoding leukocyte tyrosine kinase (LTK), is a possible candidate.

notes.statement: Li et al. (2004) found through sequence and functional analyses that NZB mice carry a gain-of-function polymorphism in the LTK kinase domain near YXXM, a binding motif for the p85 subunit of PI3K.
quotes: Sequence and functional analyses of the gene revealed that NZB has a gain-of-function polymorphism in the LTK kinase domain near YXXM, a binding motif of the p85 subunit of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K).

notes.statement: Li et al. (2004) found that SLE patients carried a similar gain-of-function type of LTK polymorphism significantly more often than healthy controls. They suggested that these polymorphic LTKs up-regulate the PI3K pathway and may form one genetic component of susceptibility to abnormal proliferation of self-reactive B cells in SLE.
quotes: SLE patients also had this type of Ltk polymorphism with a significantly higher frequency compared with the healthy controls.

Our findings suggest that these polymorphic LTKs cause up-regulation of the PI3K pathway and possibly form one genetic component of susceptibility to abnormal proliferation of self-reactive B cells in SLE.

notes.statement: Russell et al. (2004) studied CRP and APCS polymorphisms in 586 UK simplex SLE families using family-based tests and found that the less common A allele of CRP 4 (rs1205), a SNP in the 3-prime flanking/untranslated region of CRP, was over-transmitted to SLE probands (TRANSMIT P = 0.003 in all families; P = 0.0008 in 394 trios). CRP haplotype 2, carrying this allele, was associated with SLE.
quotes: We demonstrated using both haplotype analysis and single marker inheritance that the less common A allele of the single nucleotide polymorphism CRP 4 in the 3′ region of the CRP gene is associated with the development of SLE.
When trios only were studied the association with CRP 4 was stronger (143 transmissions compared with 92 non-transmissions P = 0.0008) in all 394 trios.

notes.statement: Russell et al. (2004) found that the rare allele of CRP 4 was also over-transmitted to individuals with antinuclear antibodies in the combined cohorts (P = 0.002), suggesting it may promote susceptibility to antinuclear autoimmunity; no association with renal lupus or other autoantibodies was found.
quotes: again there was a significant over-transmission of the rare allele of CRP 4 to ANA positive individuals (median of 25 TRANSMIT iterations χ2 = 12, P = 0.002).
Stratification for renal involvement in the probands (128 families in cohort 1) was negative for association/linkage between renal lupus and any pentraxin polymorphism.

notes.statement: Russell et al. (2004) showed that CRP 2 (rs1800947) and CRP 4 independently influenced basal serum CRP levels in SLE patients and their sibs, with a gene-dose effect for CRP 4; the allele associated with reduced basal CRP was the one associated with SLE, supporting the hypothesis that defective disposal of immunogenic nuclear material contributes to lupus pathogenesis.
quotes: These analyses indicated correlation with CRP 4 genotype (P = 0.003) and an independent effect from CRP 2 (P = 0.01).
inheritance of minor alleles at both SNPs predicted a CRP level of 0.9 mg/l, whereas inheritance of the common alleles at both SNP predicted a value of 3.4 mg/l.
Thus, the polymorphism associated with reduced basal CRP was also associated with the development of SLE.

notes.statement: Russell et al. (2004) found no coding polymorphisms in CRP or APCS other than synonymous changes, and APCS polymorphisms showed no significant association with SLE in single-marker analysis.
quotes: No coding polymorphisms were evident in CRP; a synonymous mutation in the third nucleotide of codon 188 (leucine), resulting from a guanine to cytosine transition at nucleotide 641, was named CRP 2.
Segregation of APCS 3 alleles was distorted in European families, but this did not reach statistical significance. Other SNPs segregated at random with no association/linkage to SLE.

notes.statement: Russell et al. (2004) reported that the A allele at CRP 4 had a frequency of about 0.3 in European and Asian-Indian populations and 0.14 in Afro-Caribbean families.
quotes: The A allele at CRP 4 had a relatively high frequency in European and Asian-Indian populations (~0.3) and was present in Afro-Caribbean families too, albeit at a lower frequency (0.14).

notes.statement: Kamat et al. (2003) noted that although the triplets were genetically identical, each manifested different clinical signs and symptoms of SLE, and they were diagnosed in reverse birth order.
quotes: Although genetically identical, each sibling manifested different clinical signs and symptoms

notes.statement: LEONHARDT (1964) carried out family studies in systemic lupus erythematosus.
quotes: FAMILY STUDIES IN SYSTEMIC LUPUS ERYTHEMATOSUS.

notes.statement: POLLAK (1964) studied antinuclear antibodies in the families of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus.
quotes: ANTINUCLEAR ANTIBODIES IN FAMILIES OF PATIENTS WITH SYSTEMIC LUPUS ERYTHEMATOSUS.

notes.statement: Nakamura et al. (2003) performed genome-wide scans in SLE-prone (NZB x NZW)F1 (B/W F1) mice and found that the region including interferon-alpha (IFN-alpha) on NZB chromosome 4 was significantly linked to anxiety-like behavior. This was confirmed by anxiety-like performance of mice carrying heterozygous NZB/NZW alleles of the susceptibility region on the NZW background.
quotes: we carried out genome-wide scans, and found that the region including interferon-alpha (IFN-alpha) on NZB chromosome 4 is significantly linked to the anxiety-like behavior seen in SLE-prone New Zealand Black (NZB) x New Zealand White (NZW) F(1) (B/W F(1)) mice
This finding was confirmed by anxiety-like performances of mice with heterozygous NZB/NZW alleles in the susceptibility region onto the NZW background.

notes.statement: Nakamura et al. (2003) found elevated neuronal IFN-alpha and corticotropin-releasing hormone levels in B/W F1 mice; blockade of the mu-1 opioid receptor or CRH receptor-1 partially overcame the anxiety-like behavior, and mu-1 opioid receptor antagonist pretreatment abolished anxiety-like behavior in IFN-alpha-treated NZW mice. They suggested that a genetically determined endogenous excess of brain IFN-alpha may underlie one aspect of anxiety-like behavior in SLE-prone mice.
quotes: In B/W F(1) mice, neuronal IFN-alpha levels were elevated, and blockade of the micro (1) opioid receptor or corticotropin-releasing hormone receptor 1, possible downstream effectors for IFN-alpha in the brain partially overcame the anxiety-like behavior seen in the B/W F(1) mice.
Furthermore, pretreatment of micro (1) opioid receptor antagonist abolished anxiety-like behaviour seen in IFN-alpha-treated NZW mice.
Our data suggest that a genetically determined endogenous excess amount of IFN-alpha in the brain may form one aspect of anxiety-like behavior seen in SLE-prone mice.

notes.statement: Baechler et al. (2003) used global gene expression profiling of peripheral blood mononuclear cells to find patterns that distinguished most SLE patients from healthy controls. About half of the patients showed dysregulated expression of IFN pathway genes.
quotes: We used global gene expression profiling of peripheral blood mononuclear cells to identify distinct patterns of gene expression that distinguish most SLE patients from healthy controls.
Strikingly, about half of the patients studied showed dysregulated expression of genes in the IFN pathway.

notes.statement: Baechler et al. (2003) found that the IFN gene expression signature marked more severe SLE involving the kidneys, hematopoietic cells, and/or the central nervous system. They suggested that this subgroup of patients may benefit from therapies targeting the IFN pathway.
quotes: this IFN gene expression "signature" served as a marker for more severe disease involving the kidneys, hematopoetic cells, and/or the central nervous system
identify a subgroup of patients who may benefit from therapies targeting the IFN pathway

notes.statement: Molokhia et al. (2003) studied 124 SLE cases and 219 matched controls living in Trinidad. They restricted the admixture analysis to 52 cases and 107 controls who reported no Indian or Chinese ancestry and typed them with 31 ancestry-informative markers. Mean west African admixture was 0.81 in cases and 0.74 in controls (P = 0.01). The risk ratio for SLE per unit change in admixture was 32.5 (95% CI 2.0-518) and changed little after adjustment for socioeconomic status (28.4, 95% CI 1.7-485).
quotes: 124 cases of SLE and 219 matched controls resident in Trinidad were studied. Analysis of admixture was restricted to 52 cases and 107 controls who reported no Indian or Chinese ancestry.

Mean west African admixture (M) was 0.81 in cases and 0.74 in controls (P=0.01). The risk ratio for SLE associated with unit change in M was estimated as 32.5 with a 95% confidence interval (CI) of 2.0-518.
Adjustment for measures of socioeconomic status (household amenities in childhood and years of education) altered this risk ratio only slightly (adjusted risk ratio: 28.4, 95% CI 1.7-485).

notes.statement: Molokhia et al. (2003) concluded that their results supported an additive genetic model for the ethnic difference in SLE risk between west Africans and Europeans. They favoured this over an environmental explanation or an overdominant model, and suggested that the responsible genes could be localized by admixture mapping.
quotes: These results support an additive genetic model for the ethnic difference in risk of SLE between west Africans and Europeans, rather than an environmental explanation or an "overdominant" model in which risk is higher in heterozygous than in homozygous individuals.
This conclusion lays a basis for localizing the genes underlying this ethnic difference in risk of SLE by admixture mapping.

notes.statement: Sun et al. (2002) found that treating Fas-deficient MRL/lpr mice with an agonistic monoclonal antibody to CD137 (2A) blocked lymphadenopathy and spontaneous autoimmune disease and prolonged survival. 2A treatment quickly increased IFN-gamma production and depleted autoreactive B cells and abnormal double-negative T cells. The authors suggested this may happen through increased apoptosis by Fas- and TNF receptor-independent mechanisms.
quotes: Here we report that treatment with an agonistic monoclonal antibody to CD137 (2A) blocks lymphadenopathy and spontaneous autoimmune diseases in Fas-deficient MRL/lpr mice, ultimately leading to their prolonged survival.

Notably, 2A treatment rapidly augments IFN-gamma production, and induces the depletion of autoreactive B cells and abnormal double-negative T cells, possibly by increasing their apoptosis through Fas- and TNF receptor-independent mechanisms.

notes.statement: Prokunina et al. (2002) analyzed 2,510 individuals, including members of 5 independent sets of families and unrelated SLE patients, for SNPs in PDCD1, the strongest candidate gene within the SLEB2 susceptibility locus previously identified in Nordic multicase families. One intronic PDCD1 SNP was associated with SLE in Europeans (12% of affected vs 5% of controls; P = 0.00001, relative risk 2.6) and in Mexicans (7% vs 2%; P = 0.0009, relative risk 3.5).
quotes: Within this locus, the programmed cell death 1 gene (PDCD1, also called PD-1) was considered the strongest candidate for association with the disease.

We show that one intronic SNP in PDCD1 is associated with development of SLE in Europeans (found in 12% of affected individuals versus 5% of controls; P = 0.00001, r.r. (relative risk) = 2.6) and Mexicans (found in 7% of affected individuals versus 2% of controls; P = 0.0009, r.r. = 3.5).

notes.statement: Prokunina et al. (2002) found that the SLE-associated allele of the intronic PDCD1 SNP altered a binding site for the transcription factor RUNX1 (AML1) located in an intronic enhancer, suggesting a mechanism through which it could contribute to the development of SLE.
quotes: The associated allele of this SNP alters a binding site for the runt-related transcription factor 1 (RUNX1, also called AML1) located in an intronic enhancer, suggesting a mechanism through which it can contribute to the development of SLE in humans.

notes.statement: Prokunina et al. (2002) described SLE as a complex autoimmune disease affecting 0.05% of the Western population, predominantly women.
quotes: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE, OMIM 152700) is a complex autoimmune disease that affects 0.05% of the Western population, predominantly women.

notes.statement: Scofield et al. (2003) chose 38 pedigrees with an SLE patient who had thrombocytopenia out of 184 SLE multiplex pedigrees. They found linkage at 1q22-23 in these 38 pedigrees (maximum lod = 3.71) and at 11p13 in the 13 African American pedigrees (maximum lod = 5.72).
quotes: We selected the 38 pedigrees that had an SLE patient with thrombocytopenia (platelets, < 10 x 10(9)/L [< 100,000/microL]) from a collection of 184 pedigrees multiplex for SLE.
Linkages were established at 1q22-23 (maximum logarithm of odds [lod(max)] = 3.71) in the 38 pedigrees and at 11p13 (lod(max) = 5.72) in the 13 African American pedigrees.

notes.statement: Scofield et al. (2003) found that thrombocytopenia in SLE was associated with nephritis, serositis, neuropsychiatric involvement, autoimmune hemolytic anemia, anti-double-stranded DNA, and antiphospholipid antibody. SLE was more severe in families that had a thrombocytopenic SLE patient, whether or not an individual patient had thrombocytopenia. The authors concluded that thrombocytopenia is part of a severe familial form of SLE.
quotes: Nephritis, serositis, neuropsychiatric involvement, autoimmune hemolytic anemia, anti-double-stranded DNA, and antiphospholipid antibody were associated with thrombocytopenia.
Other results show that SLE is more severe in the families with a thrombocytopenic SLE patient, whether or not thrombocytopenia in an individual patient is considered.
These results are consistent with thrombocytopenia being a component of a severe familial form of SLE and with genes at 1q22-23 and 11p13 contributing to this severe phenotype

notes.statement: Johanneson et al. (2002) genotyped 87 multicase SLE families from European and recently admixed American populations for 62 chromosome 1 microsatellite markers. Parametric two-point linkage analysis identified six regions (1p36, 1p21, 1q23, 1q25, 1q31, and 1q43) with LOD scores of 1.50 or higher, all previously described, with contributions that differed by the families' population of origin.
quotes: By parametric two-point linkage analysis, six regions (1p36, 1p21, 1q23, 1q25, 1q31, and 1q43) were identified that have LOD scores of Z>or=1.50, with different contributions, depending on the population of origin of the families (European or admixed American).

notes.statement: Johanneson et al. (2002) found a significant three-point LOD score of 3.79 at 1q31. Families from all populations contributed to this result, with several markers and under the same parametric model. The authors concluded that the 1q31 locus contains a major susceptibility gene for SLE in general populations.
quotes: The locus at 1q31 showed a significant three-point LOD score of Z=3.79 and was contributed by families from all populations, with several markers and under the same parametric model.
We conclude that the locus at 1q31 contains a major susceptibility gene, important to SLE in general populations.

notes.statement: Johanneson et al. (2002) analyzed a known mutation in the CD45 gene in their SLE families and found that the results did not support a role for this mutation in the disease.
quotes: Analysis of a known mutation in the CD45 gene did not support the role that this mutation plays in disease.

notes.statement: Kelly et al. (2002) noted that SLE showed familial aggregation, with lambda(s) estimates of 10 to 20 and a monozygotic twin concordance rate greater than 20%.
quotes: With lambda(s) estimates of 10 to 20 and other evidence of familial aggregation, as well as a monozygotic twin concordance rate >20, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) would appear to be a very promising phenotype using modern genetic approaches.

notes.statement: Kelly et al. (2002) reviewed completed linkage studies in SLE multiplex pedigrees, which had identified 60 susceptibility loci; 7 met or exceeded the threshold for significant linkage (LOD at least 3.3 or P at most 0.00005): 1q22-q23, 1q41, 2q37, 4p16, 6p21-p11, 16q13, and 17p13. Linkages at 1q41, 4p16, and 6p21 had been independently confirmed, with additional suggestive evidence for 1q22-q23 and 2q37.
quotes: The completed genetic linkage studies performed on various collections of pedigrees multiplex for SLE have identified 60 susceptibility loci with varying degrees of evidence for linkage in man.
Seven of these meet or exceed the threshold for significant linkage (LOD > or = 3.3 or P < or = 0.00005) at 1q22-23, 1q41, 2q37, 4p16, 6p21-11, 16q13 and 17p13.

Evidence that these linkages can be reproduced range from outright independent confirmation (1q41, 4p16 and 6p21) to additional suggestive evidence in the genomic region of the purported linkage (1q22-23 and 2q37).

notes.statement: Kelly et al. (2002) observed that SLE linkages usually dominated in one ethnicity or another, suggesting that the responsible polymorphisms, once identified, would also vary by ethnicity.
quotes: In addition, these linkages usually dominate in one ethnicity or another, suggesting that the responsible polymorphisms, once identified, will also vary by ethnicity.

notes.statement: Kelly et al. (2002) reviewed known genetic associations with SLE at candidate loci, including various HLA alleles, complement component genes, and Fc-gamma receptors, and noted that murine lupus models had provided additional candidate genes and potential syntenic linkages.
quotes: genetic associations are already known at numerous candidate loci including various HLA alleles, complement component genes, Fcgamma receptors, and others, and murine genetic studies of lupus models have provided additional candidate genes and potential syntenic linkages to evaluate in man.

notes.statement: Quintero-Del-Rio et al. (2002) analyzed genome scan data from more than 300 microsatellite markers in 75 SLE pedigrees with at least 1 SLE patient who met the ACR renal criterion. In European-American pedigrees they found a maximum screening lod score of 3.16 at 10q22.3, and multipoint sib-pair regression gave P = 0.0000008 at this locus, which they called SLEN1.
quotes: we evaluated genome scan data from >300 microsatellite markers in the 75 pedigrees that had at least one SLE affected with the SLE renal criterion. A maximum-likelihood parametric model approach produced a maximum screening LOD score of 3.16 at 10q22.3 in the European-American (EA) pedigrees.
A multipoint sib-pair regression analysis produced P = 0.0000008 in EA at 10q22.3 (SLEN1) and P = 0.000001 in AA at 2q34-35 (SLEN2).

notes.statement: In African American pedigrees with renal disease, Quintero-Del-Rio et al. (2002) found linkage to 2q34-35 by sib-pair analysis (P = 0.000001), which they called SLEN2. They also found a maximum screening lod score of 2.58 at 11p15.6.
quotes: The African-American (AA) pedigrees obtained a maximum screening LOD score of 2.58 at 11p15.6.
A multipoint sib-pair regression analysis produced P = 0.0000008 in EA at 10q22.3 (SLEN1) and P = 0.000001 in AA at 2q34-35 (SLEN2).

notes.statement: In 35 pedigrees with 2 or more SLE patients with renal disease, Quintero-Del-Rio et al. (2002) obtained a lod score of 3.34 at 11p15.6 in African American families, which they called SLEN3. Sib-pair analysis in these pedigrees also suggested linkage at 4q13.1 in European Americans (P = 0.00003) and at 11p13 (P = 0.00003) and 3q23 (P = 0.00007) in African Americans.
quotes: A second stratification strategy explored the renal criterion in 35 pedigrees with two or more SLE patients with renal disease and produced a LOD score of 3.34 at 11p15.6 in AA (SLEN3).
Sib-pair analysis in these 35 pedigrees revealed P = 0.00003 at 4q13.1 in EA, P = 0.00003 at 11p13 and 0.00007 at 3q23 in AA.

notes.statement: Quintero-Del-Rio et al. (2002) concluded that multiple genetic linkages are related to the renal criterion in SLE. They noted that the linkages at 10q22.3 in European Americans (SLEN1) and at 2q34-35 in African Americans (SLEN2) had not been described before.
quotes: Thus, multiple genetic linkages are related to the renal criterion in SLE.
those at 10q22.3 in the EA pedigrees (SLEN1) and at 2q34-35 in the AA pedigrees (SLEN2) have not been previously described.

notes.statement: Quintero-Del-Rio et al. (2002) noted that renal disease occurs in 40 to 75% of SLE patients and contributes significantly to morbidity and mortality.
quotes: Renal disease occurs in 40-75% of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) patients and significantly contributes to morbidity and mortality.

notes.statement: Graham et al. (2002) mapped the HLA region with a dense set of polymorphic microsatellites in a large collection of families with SLE. They identified 3 distinct haplotypes that covered the class II region and showed transmission distortion. DRB1 and DQB1 typing of founders showed that these haplotypes carried DRB1*1501/DQB1*0602, DRB1*0801/DQB1*0402, and DRB1*0301/DQB1*0201.
quotes: Using a dense map of polymorphic microsatellites across the HLA region in a large collection of families with SLE, we identified three distinct haplotypes that encompassed the class II region and exhibited transmission distortion.
DRB1 and DQB1 typing of founders showed that the three haplotypes contained DRB1*1501/ DQB1*0602, DRB1*0801/ DQB1*0402, and DRB1*0301/DQB1*0201 alleles, respectively.

notes.statement: By visualizing ancestral recombinants, Graham et al. (2002) narrowed the disease-associated haplotypes containing DRB1*1501 and DRB1*0801 to a region of approximately 500 kb. They concluded that HLA class II haplotypes containing DRB1 and DQB1 alleles are strong risk factors for human SLE.
quotes: By visualizing ancestral recombinants, we narrowed the disease-associated haplotypes containing DRB1*1501 and DRB1*0801 to an approximately 500-kb region.
We conclude that HLA class II haplotypes containing DRB1 and DQB1 alleles are strong risk factors for human SLE.

notes.statement: Kyogoku et al. (2002) screened FCGR2B for variants and found a SNP, c.695T>C, that causes an ile232-to-thr (I232T) substitution in the transmembrane domain. In 193 Japanese SLE patients and 303 healthy controls, the 232T/T genotype was significantly more frequent in patients.
quotes: We detected a single-nucleotide polymorphism in FCGR2B, (c.695T>C), coding for a nonsynonymous substitution, Ile232Thr (I232T), within the transmembrane domain. The frequency of the 232T/T genotype was significantly increased in SLE patients compared with healthy individuals.

notes.statement: Kyogoku et al. (2002) found that FCGR3A-176F/F was significantly associated with SLE in Japanese patients. Two-locus analyses suggested that both FCGR2B and FCGR3A may contribute to susceptibility. The authors considered the previously reported FCGR3B association to be secondary, arising from strong linkage disequilibrium with FCGR2B.
quotes: FCGR3A-176F/F showed significant association. Two-locus analyses suggested that both FCGR2B and FCGR3A may contribute to SLE susceptibility, while the previously reported association of FCGR3B was considered to be secondary and derived from strong linkage disequilibrium with FCGR2B.

notes.statement: Leadbetter et al. (2002) showed that IgG2a-chromatin immune complexes effectively activated rheumatoid factor-positive B cells. This activation required the synergistic engagement of the antigen receptor and a member of the MyD88-dependent Toll-like receptor family, and inhibitor studies implicated TLR9. The authors concluded that this links innate and adaptive immunity in the development of systemic autoimmune disease and explains the preponderance of autoantibodies reactive with nucleic acid-protein particles.
quotes: Here we show that effective activation of RF+ B cells is mediated by IgG2a-chromatin immune complexes and requires the synergistic engagement of the antigen receptor and a member of the MyD88-dependent Toll-like receptor (TLR) family. Inhibitor studies implicate TLR9.

These data establish a critical link between the innate and adaptive immune systems in the development of systemic autoimmune disease and explain the preponderance of autoantibodies reactive with nucleic acid-protein particles.

notes.statement: Stein et al. (2002) studied 372 affected individuals from 160 multiplex SLE pedigrees, 25 of which contained at least 1 affected male. Renal disease was significantly more frequent in female family members who had an affected male relative than in those who did not (68% vs 43%; P = 0.002). This trend remained after stratification by race and was most pronounced in European Americans.
quotes: The presence of renal disease was significantly increased in female family members with an affected male relative when compared with those with no affected male relative (68% and 43%, respectively; P = 0.002).
This trend remained after stratifying by race and was most pronounced in European Americans.

notes.statement: Stein et al. (2002) concluded that the increased prevalence of renal disease previously reported in men with SLE is, in large part, a familial rather than a sex-based difference, at least in multiplex SLE families. A familial basis was also suggested for differences in hematologic and immunologic manifestations, whereas arthritis and dermatologic features appeared to be influenced mostly by sex.
quotes: Our results demonstrate that the increased prevalence of renal disease previously reported in men with SLE is, in large part, a familial rather than sex-based difference, at least in multiplex SLE families.
A familial basis for differences in hematologic and immunologic manifestations was also suggested, while arthritis and dermatologic features appeared to be most influenced by sex.

notes.statement: Blanco et al. (2001) found that blood monocytes from SLE patients worked as antigen-presenting cells in vitro. Serum from SLE patients made normal monocytes differentiate into dendritic cells, which could capture antigens from dying cells and present them to CD4-positive T cells.
quotes: monocytes from SLE patients' blood were found to function as antigen-presenting cells, in vitro. Furthermore, serum from SLE patients induced normal monocytes to differentiate into DCs. These DCs could capture antigens from dying cells and present them to CD4-positive T cells.

notes.statement: Blanco et al. (2001) found that how strongly SLE patient serum induced dendritic cell differentiation correlated with disease activity and depended on interferon-alpha. They proposed that unchecked induction of dendritic cells by IFN-alpha may drive the autoimmune response in SLE.
quotes: The capacity of SLE patients' serum to induce DC differentiation correlated with disease activity and depended on the actions of interferon-alpha (IFN-alpha). Thus, unabated induction of DCs by IFN-alpha may drive the autoimmune response in SLE.

notes.statement: DeGiorgio et al. (2001) found that the pentapeptide Asp/Glu-Trp-Asp/Glu-Tyr-Ser/Gly, a molecular mimic of double-stranded DNA, is also present in the extracellular domain of the NMDA receptor subunits NR2a and NR2b. Both murine and human anti-DNA antibodies recognized the NR2 receptor, and anti-DNA antibodies with this cross-reactivity caused apoptotic death of neurons in vivo and in vitro.
quotes: This sequence is also present in the extracellular domain of murine and human NMDA (N-methyl-D-aspartate) receptor subunits NR2a and NR2b.

Here we show that the NR2 receptor is recognized by both murine and human anti-DNA antibodies. Moreover, anti-DNA antibodies with this cross-reactivity mediate apoptotic death of neurons in vivo and in vitro.

notes.statement: DeGiorgio et al. (2001) found these cross-reactive antibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid of a patient with SLE, and the fluid caused neuronal apoptosis. They concluded that lupus antibodies that cross-react with DNA and NMDA receptors can enter the cerebrospinal fluid. They suggested these antibodies may cause CNS abnormalities that are not due to thrombosis or vasculitis.
quotes: These observations indicate that lupus antibodies cross-react with DNA and NMDA receptors, gain access to cerebrospinal fluid and may mediate non-thrombotic and non-vasculitic abnormalities of the central nervous system.

notes.statement: Yasutomo et al. (2001) found that their data were consistent with the hypothesis that low DNASE1 activity is directly connected to the progression of human SLE, noting that mice deficient in Dnase1 develop an SLE-like syndrome.
quotes: Mice deficient in deoxyribonuclease I (Dnase1) develop an SLE-like syndrome.
These data are consistent with the hypothesis that a direct connection exists between low activity of DNASE1 and progression of human SLE.

notes.statement: Solomou et al. (2001) found that nuclear extracts from unstimulated T cells of patients with SLE, unlike those from normal T cells, contained increased amounts of phosphorylated cAMP-responsive element modulator (p-CREM), which bound the -180 site of the IL-2 promoter. After stimulation, normal T cells showed increased binding of phosphorylated CREB (p-CREB) to this site, whereas SLE T cells showed mainly p-CREM binding and less p-CREB binding.
quotes: nuclear extracts from unstimulated SLE T cells, unlike extracts from normal T cells, express increased amounts of phosphorylated cAMP-responsive element modulator (p-CREM) that binds the -180 site of the IL-2 promoter
whereas nuclear extracts from stimulated SLE T cells display primarily p-CREM and decreased p-CREB binding

notes.statement: In SLE T cells, Solomou et al. (2001) found that p-CREM bound the transcriptional coactivators CREB-binding protein and p300, and that increased p-CREM expression correlated with decreased IL-2 production. A reporter gene driven by the -180 site was transcribed more in normal T cells but was suppressed in SLE T cells. The authors concluded that transcriptional repression is responsible for the decreased IL-2 production by SLE T cells.
quotes: In SLE T cells, p-CREM bound to the transcriptional coactivators, CREB binding protein and p300. Increased expression of p-CREM correlated with decreased production of IL-2.
The transcription of a reporter gene driven by the -180 site was enhanced in normal T cells, but was suppressed in SLE T cells.
These experiments demonstrate that transcriptional repression is responsible for the decreased production of IL-2 by SLE T cells.

notes.statement: Linker-Israeli et al. (1999) genotyped the AT-rich minisatellite in the 3-prime flanking region and the 5-prime promoter-enhancer of the IL6 gene in 146 SLE patients and 139 controls. The minisatellite allele distribution differed significantly between patients and controls in both Caucasians and African Americans. Short alleles (792 bp or less) were seen only in SLE patients, and the 828-bp allele was over-represented in controls. SLE showed no preferential association with the G/C alleles in the 5-prime region.
quotes: The AT-rich minisatellite allele distribution pattern was significantly different in SLE (n = 146) as compared to 139 controls (chi 2(7) = 48.97, P = 0.001, Caucasians; and chi 2(7) = 19.93, P = 0.006, African-Americans).
In either race, short allele sizes (< or = 792 bp) were seen exclusively in SLE patients (P = 0.001), whereas the 828-bp allele was over-represented in controls (P = 0.015 and 0.002).
In contrast, there was no preferential association of SLE with G/C alleles in the 5' region of the IL-6 gene.

notes.statement: Linker-Israeli et al. (1999) found that B lymphoblastoid cells from patients carrying one or two SLE-associated IL6 3-prime minisatellite alleles secreted 3- to 4-fold more IL-6 than cells without these alleles. Individuals with these alleles also had about 4-fold higher percentages of IL-6-positive monocytes. In lupus patients carrying these alleles, IL-6 mRNA stability was significantly increased, which suggested that the alleles are biologically significant.
quotes: B lymphoblastoid cells of patients having one or two SLE-associated alleles secreted IL-6 in 3- to 4-fold higher levels than non-allelic cells (P < 0.05)
higher percentages (approximately 4-fold) of IL-6 positive monocytes were observed in individuals having SLE-associated IL-6 alleles
in lupus patients having SLE-associated minisatellite alleles, IL-6 mRNA stability was significantly enhanced

notes.statement: Zhang et al. (2001) found significantly raised levels of B lymphocyte stimulator (BLyS) in the serum of patients with SLE. The BLyS isolated from patient sera had the same molecular weight as the natural soluble form and stimulated B-cell activation in vitro.
quotes: Here, we demonstrate significant elevations of BLyS in the patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).
The BLyS isolated from the sera of SLE patients had the same m.w. as the natural soluble form and was able to stimulate B cell activation in vitro.

notes.statement: Zhang et al. (2001) found that raised BLyS in SLE patients was partially associated with higher levels of IgG, IgM, and IgA anti-dsDNA antibodies but not with disease activity. They suggested that BLyS may be a useful marker for early activation of an autoimmune diathesis and likely plays a critical role in triggering self-antigen-driven autoimmune B cells.
quotes: Increased BLyS in SLE patients was partially associated with higher levels of anti-dsDNA Ab of the IgG, IgM, and IgA classes, but not associated with the disease activity.

Our results suggest that BLyS may be a useful marker for early activation of an autoimmune diathesis and likely plays a critical role in triggering activation of self-Ag-driven autoimmune B cells in human SLE.

notes.statement: Zhang et al. (2001) proposed that BLyS may be an effective therapeutic target in systemic autoimmunity.
quotes: BLyS may provide an effective therapeutic target in systemic autoimmunity.

notes.statement: In a genome scan of 126 pedigrees multiplex for SLE, including 469 sib pairs (affected and unaffected) and 175 affected relative pairs, Gray-McGuire et al. (2000) found a novel linkage to chromosome 4p16-15.2 (P = 0.0003 and lod = 3.84) using revised multipoint Haseman-Elston regression and conditional logistic regression. They confirmed linkage to 4p16-15.2 in European American families using an independent pedigree collection.
quotes: We present here the results of a genome scan of 126 pedigrees multiplex for SLE, including 469 sibling pairs (affected and unaffected) and 175 affected relative pairs.
we identify a novel linkage to chromosome 4p16-15.2 (P=.0003 and LOD=3.84)
We confirm the evidence of linkage to chromosome 4p16-15.2 in European American families using data from an independent pedigree collection.

notes.statement: Gray-McGuire et al. (2000) presented evidence of an epistatic interaction between chromosome 4p16-15.2 and chromosome 5p15 in European American SLE families.
quotes: present evidence of an epistatic interaction between chromosome 4p16-15.2 and chromosome 5p15 in our European American families

notes.statement: Gray-McGuire et al. (2000) found that their data supported the published results of 3 independent studies for 9 purportedly linked SLE regions and agreed with previously published results from a subset of these data for 3 regions.
quotes: our data support the published results of three independent studies for nine purportedly linked regions and agree with the previously published results from a subset of these data for three regions

notes.statement: Napirei et al. (2000) generated Dnase1-deficient mice by gene targeting and found that they showed classical symptoms of SLE, namely antinuclear antibodies, deposition of immune complexes in glomeruli, and full-blown glomerulonephritis, in a Dnase1 dose-dependent manner. The authors suggested that lack or reduction of DNASE1 is a critical factor in the initiation of human SLE.
quotes: we have generated Dnase1-deficient mice by gene targeting. We report here that these animals show the classical symptoms of SLE, namely the presence of ANA, the deposition of immune complexes in glomeruli and full-blown glomerulonephritis in a Dnase1-dose-dependent manner.
Our findings suggest that lack or reduction of Dnase1 is a critical factor in the initiation of human SLE.

notes.statement: Napirei et al. (2000) found serum DNASE1 activities to be lower in SLE patients than in normal subjects, in agreement with earlier reports.
quotes: Moreover, in agreement with earlier reports, we found Dnase1 activities in serum to be lower in SLE patients than in normal subjects.

notes.statement: Gross et al. (2000) found that transgenic mice overexpressing zTNF4 (BLyS/BAFF) in lymphoid cells developed symptoms characteristic of SLE and expanded a rare population of splenic B-1a lymphocytes. Circulating zTNF4 was more abundant in NZBWF1 and MRL-lpr/lpr mice during the onset and progression of SLE.
quotes: Transgenic animals overexpressing zTNF4 in lymphoid cells develop symptoms characteristic of systemic lupus erythaematosus (SLE) and expand a rare population of splenic B-Ia lymphocytes.
circulating zTNF4 is more abundant in NZBWF1 and MRL-lpr/lpr mice during the onset and progression of SLE.

notes.statement: Gross et al. (2000) identified TACI and BCMA as receptors for zTNF4. Treating NZBWF1 mice with a soluble TACI-Ig fusion protein inhibited the development of proteinuria and prolonged survival. The authors suggested TACI-Ig as a promising treatment for autoimmune disease in humans.
quotes: We have identified two TNF receptor family members, TACI and BCMA, that bind zTNF4.
Treatment of NZBWF1 mice with soluble TACI-Ig fusion protein inhibits the development of proteinuria and prolongs survival of the animals.
identify TACI-Ig as a promising treatment of autoimmune disease in humans.

notes.statement: Gaffney et al. (2000) ran a second genome screen in 82 new SLE sib-pair families. The four best intervals were 7p22 (lod score 2.87), 7q21 (lod 2.40), 10p13 (lod 2.24) and 7q36 (lod 2.15). Eight more intervals had lod scores of 1.00 to 1.67.
quotes: In the cohort 2 screen, the four best intervals were 7p22 (LOD score 2.87), 7q21 (LOD score 2.40), 10p13 (LOD score 2.24), and 7q36 (LOD score 2.15). Eight additional intervals were identified with LOD scores in the range 1.00-1.67.

notes.statement: In a combined analysis of 187 SLE sib-pair families from 2 Minnesota cohorts, Gaffney et al. (2000) found significant linkage at 6p11-p21 (D6S426, lod score 4.19) and at 16q13 (D16S415, lod score 3.85). The intervals 2p15, 7q36 and 1q42 had lod scores of 1.92 to 2.06, and 13 other intervals had lod scores of 1.00 to 1.78.
quotes: A combined analysis of MN cohorts 1 and 2 (187 sib-pair families) showed that markers in 6p11-p21 (D6S426, LOD score 4.19) and 16q13 (D16S415, LOD score 3.85) met the criteria for significant linkage.
Three intervals (2p15, 7q36, and 1q42) had LOD scores in the range 1.92-2.06, and another 13 intervals had LOD scores in the range of 1.00-1.78 in the combined sample.

notes.statement: Lindqvist et al. (2000) performed genome scans in families with multiple SLE patients from Iceland and Sweden. In the Icelandic families, 5 regions had lod scores greater than 2.0: 4p15-p13 (Z = 3.20), 9p22 (Z = 2.27), 19q13 (Z = 2.06), 19p13 (D19S247, Z = 2.58), and 2q37 (D2S125, Z = 2.06). The first 3 are homologous to murine regions containing the lmb2, sle2, and sle3 loci.
quotes: we performed genome scans in families with multiple SLE patients from Iceland, a geographical and genetic isolate, and from Sweden

In the Icelandic families, five regions showed lod scores greater than 2.0, three of which (4p15-13, Z=3.20; 9p22, Z=2.27; 19q13, Z=2.06) are homologous to the murine regions containing the lmb2, sle2 and sle3 loci, respectively.
The fourth region is located on 19p13 (D19S247, Z=2.58) and the fifth on 2q37 (D2S125, Z=2.06).

notes.statement: In the Swedish families, Lindqvist et al. (2000) found only 2 regions with lod scores above 2.0: 2q11 (D2S436, Z = 2.13) and 2q37 (D2S125, Z = 2.18). When the 2 family sets were combined, the lod score at D2S125 was 4.24, supporting linkage to 2q37. The authors concluded that this region was a new SLE locus (hSLE1).
quotes: Only two regions showed lod scores above 2.0 in the Swedish families: on chromosome 2q11 (D2S436, Z=2. 13) and 2q37 (D2S125, Z=2.18).
The combination of both family sets gave a highly significant lod score at D2S125 of Z=4.24 in favor of linkage for 2q37. This region represents a new locus for SLE.

notes.statement: Lessard et al. (1999) gave single oral doses of procainamide to 13 CYP2D6 extensive metabolizers and 6 poor metabolizers. They found urinary nitroprocainamide in 7 of the 13 extensive metabolizers and in none of the poor metabolizers. No subject had detectable nitroprocainamide while taking the CYP2D6 inhibitor quinidine. The authors suggested that CYP2D6 is involved in the N-oxidation of procainamide in vivo, a pathway that produces a metabolite that may be involved in procainamide-induced lupus. They said further studies were needed to show whether low CYP2D6 activity could prevent the syndrome.
quotes: the urinary excretion of nitroprocainamide during period 1 was measurable in 7/13 extensive metabolizers but in none of the poor metabolizers
our results suggest that CYP2D6 is involved in the in-vivo aliphatic amine deethylation and N-oxidation of procainamide at its arylamine function in man
Further studies are needed to demonstrate whether a low CYP2D6 activity, either genetically determined or pharmacologically modulated, could prevent drug-induced lupus erythematosus syndrome

notes.statement: Mohan et al. (1999) found that B6.NZMc1|c7 mice, which are bicongenic for the NZM2410-derived lupus nephritis susceptibility loci Sle1 and Sle3, had splenomegaly and expanded populations of activated B cells and CD4+ T cells. They also had a strong, varied IgG autoantibody response against chromatin (including dsDNA), intact glomeruli and basement membrane matrix antigens. These mice, particularly the females, had highly penetrant glomerulonephritis. In contrast, mice monocongenic for Sle1 lost tolerance to chromatin but did not develop disease, and mice monocongenic for Sle3 had only mildly penetrant glomerulonephritis.
quotes: the present study reveals that B6.NZMc1|c7 mice, bicongenic for Sle1 and Sle3, exhibit splenomegaly, significantly expanded populations of activated B and CD4(+) T cells, and a robust, variegated IgG autoantibody response targeting multiple components of chromatin (including double-stranded DNA), intact glomeruli, and basement membrane matrix antigens.
As one might predict, these mice, particularly the females, exhibit highly penetrant glomerulonephritis.

notes.statement: Mohan et al. (1999) proposed a two-step epistatic model for how pathogenic, kidney-targeting autoantibodies form in lupus. In this model, loci such as Sle1 break tolerance to chromatin, while full pathogenic maturation of the autoantibody response appears to require input from other loci, such as Sle3, and from gender-based factors.
quotes: These findings lend strong support to a two-step epistatic model for the formation of pathogenic, nephrophilic autoantibodies in lupus.

Whereas loci such as Sle1 may serve to breach tolerance to chromatin, full-blown pathogenic maturation of the autoantibody response appears to require additional input from other loci (such as Sle3) and gender-based factors.

notes.statement: Kelly et al. (1999) reported a male infant who had chondrodysplasia punctata (stippled epiphyses) and developed a typical lupus erythematosus rash. The infant's skin findings led to a diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus in his mother. The authors reviewed the literature supporting maternal lupus as one cause of chondrodysplasia punctata.
quotes: The skin abnormalities in the infant resulted in a diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus in his mother.
The differential diagnosis of chondrodysplasia punctata and the literature supporting maternal lupus as one cause are reviewed.
