notes.statement: Shai et al. (1999) performed a genome-wide screen with 350 polymorphic markers (average spacing 12 cM) in 188 SLE patients from 80 multiplex families. Nonparametric multipoint linkage analysis suggested evidence for predisposing loci on chromosomes 1 and 18.
quotes: using the ABI Prism linkage mapping set which includes 350 polymorphic markers with an average spacing of 12 cM
Non-parametric multipoint linkage analysis suggests evidence for predisposing loci on chromosomes 1 and 18.

notes.statement: Shai et al. (1999) found clear support for loci in the 1q44 and 1p36 regions only in Mexican American SLE families, not in Caucasian families. They suggested that each ethnic group should be considered separately.
quotes: the support for a gene in the 1q44 region as well as in the 1p36 region is clearly found only in the Mexican American families with SLE but not in families of Caucasian ethnicity

notes.statement: Shai et al. (1999) found no single locus with overwhelming evidence for linkage. They suggested that no 'major' susceptibility genes segregate in SLE families and that the genetic etiology more likely involves several genes of moderate effect.
quotes: no single locus with overwhelming evidence for linkage was found, suggesting that there are no 'major' susceptibility genes segregating in families with SLE, and that the genetic etiology is more likely to result from the action of several genes of moderate effect

notes.statement: Gaffney et al. (1998) performed a genome-wide microsatellite screen in 105 SLE sib-pair families. Using multipoint nonparametric methods, the strongest evidence for linkage was near the HLA locus on 6p11-p21 (D6S257, lod = 3.90), with additional regions at 16q13 (D16S415, lod = 3.64), 14q21-q23 (D14S276, lod = 2.81), and 20p12 (D20S186, lod = 2.62).
quotes: the strongest evidence for linkage was found near the HLA locus (6p11-p21) [D6S257, logarithm of odds (lod) = 3.90, P = 0.000011] and at three additional regions: 16q13 (D16S415, lod = 3.64, P = 0.000022), 14q21-23 (D14S276, lod = 2.81, P = 0.00016), and 20p12 (D20S186, lod = 2.62, P = 0.00025).

notes.statement: Gaffney et al. (1998) identified 9 further regions with lod scores of 1.00 or greater: 1p36, 1p13, 1q42, 2p15, 2q21-q33, 3cen-q11, 4q28, 11p15, and 15q26.
quotes: Another nine regions (1p36, 1p13, 1q42, 2p15, 2q21-33, 3cent-q11, 4q28, 11p15, and 15q26) were identified with lod scores >/=1.00.

notes.statement: Gaffney et al. (1998) concluded that their data supported the hypothesis that multiple genes, including one in the HLA region, influence susceptibility to human SLE.
quotes: These data support the hypothesis that multiple genes, including one in the HLA region, influence susceptibility to human SLE.

notes.statement: Toriello (1998) reported chondrodysplasia punctata in association with maternal systemic lupus erythematosus.
quotes: Chondrodysplasia punctata and maternal systemic lupus erythematosus.

notes.statement: Austin-Ward et al. (1998) reported a newborn whose mother had been diagnosed with SLE before the pregnancy. The infant had neonatal lupus, chondrodysplasia punctata and other findings that looked like the birth defects linked to oral anticoagulants, although there was no history of exposure. The authors speculated that the combined action of the mother's different autoantibodies may produce the whole spectrum of manifestations.
quotes: The child had clinical manifestations of neonatal lupus as well as chondrodysplasia punctata and other findings that resemble the congenital anomalies associated with the use of oral anticoagulants, with no history of exposure.
We speculate that the combined action of the different maternal autoantibodies may produce the whole spectrum of manifestations.

notes.statement: Elçioglu and Hall (1998) described two sibs with chondrodysplasia punctata whose mother had systemic lupus erythematosus, along with the sibs' radiologic features. After comparing them with other forms of chondrodysplasia punctata, they highlighted a possible association between the skeletal phenotype and maternal SLE.
quotes: Two sibs with chondrodysplasia punctata in whom the mother was suffering from systemic lupus erythematosus are presented and the radiological features described.
the possible association with maternal systemic lupus erythematosus is highlighted

notes.statement: García et al. (1996) studied autoantibody profiles in 222 African-American SLE patients, 94 with lupus nephritis and 128 without. Only anti-dsDNA antibodies differed significantly between the two groups. The authors concluded that African-American SLE patients with lupus nephritis do not have a specific or distinctive autoantibody profile.
quotes: Only anti-dsDNA achieved statistical significance between the two groups (P < 0.05).
We conclude that African-American SLE patients with LN do not exhibit a specific or distinctive autoantibody profile. However, our data confirm the value of anti-dsDNA in SLE patients with LN.

notes.statement: Sanghera et al. (1997) identified 2 common missense mutations in the fifth domain of apolipoprotein H (beta-2-glycoprotein I), trp316-to-ser and cys306-to-gly. ApoH from Ser316 homozygotes and Ser316/Gly306 compound heterozygotes did not bind phosphatidylserine. The authors suggested that about 2 million compound heterozygous Caucasians in the United States might be unable to produce apoH-dependent antiphospholipid autoantibodies.
quotes: ApoH from the two homozygotes (Ser316/Ser316) and all seven compound heterozygotes (Ser316/Gly306) failed to bind to PS; all heterozygotes at one or the other sites and wild type showed normal PS binding.
An estimated 2 million Caucasians in the United States, who are compound heterozygotes for the two mutations, may be precluded from producing apoH-dependent antiphospholipid autoantibodies.

notes.statement: Vyse et al. (1996) studied (NZB x NZW)F1 x NZW backcross mice, a model of human SLE. They found that one set of loci coordinately regulated serum levels of IgG antibodies to double-stranded DNA, single-stranded DNA, total histones, and chromatin, and that these loci overlapped with loci linked to production of autoantibodies to the viral glycoprotein gp70.
quotes: We used a genetic analysis of (NZB x NZW)F1 x NZW backcross mice to provide insight into whether different autoantibodies are subject to separate genetic influences

The results showed one set of loci that coordinately regulated serum levels of IgG antibodies to double-stranded DNA, single-stranded DNA, total histones, and chromatin, which overlapped with loci that were linked to the production of autoantibodies to the viral glycoprotein, gp70.

notes.statement: Vyse et al. (1996) found that loci linked with anti-gp70 antibodies showed stronger linkage with renal disease than those linked with antinuclear antibodies, suggesting that anti-gp70 autoantibodies are the major pathogenic antibodies in this mouse model of lupus nephritis. A distal chromosome 4 locus, Nba1, was linked with nephritis but not with any measured autoantibody, suggesting that it acts at a checkpoint distal to autoantibody production.
quotes: Loci linked with anti-gp70 compared with antinuclear antibodies demonstrated the strongest linkage with renal disease, suggesting that autoantibodies to gp70 are the major pathogenic antibodies in this model of lupus nephritis.

a distal chromosome 4 locus, Nba1, was linked with nephritis but not with any of the autoantibodies measured, suggesting that it contributes to renal disease at a checkpoint distal to autoantibody production.

notes.statement: Wu et al. (1996) screened DNA from 75 patients with SLE by SSCP analysis of the FasL extracellular domain and found a heterozygous variant in only 1 patient. They suggested that FASL mutations are an uncommon cause of SLE.
quotes: DNA from 75 patients with SLE was screened by single-stranded conformational polymorphism analysis for potential mutations of the extracellular domain of FasL.
suggests that fasL mutations are an uncommon cause of the disease

notes.statement: Wu et al. (1996) found that PBMCs from an SLE patient carrying a FASL in-frame deletion showed decreased FasL activity, decreased activation-induced cell death, and increased T-cell proliferation after activation. This was the first report of defective FasL-mediated apoptosis linked to a human FASL mutation in SLE.
quotes: Analysis of PBMC from this patient revealed decreased FasL activity, decreased activation-induced cell death, and increased T cell proliferation after activation.
This is the first report of defective FasL-mediated apoptosis related to a mutation of the human Fasl, gene in a patient with SLE

notes.statement: Sibley et al. (1993) described a family in which 3 members developed SLE complicated by ischemic vasculopathy (digital ischemia), with remarkably similar calendar years and ages of onset and clinical courses despite differing genotypes, and discussed the potential contributions of heredity and environment to the concordance.
quotes: The calendar years and patient ages of disease onset and the clinical courses were remarkably similar for all 3 patients, although their genotypes were not.
The potential contributions of heredity and environment to the concordance of disease expression in this family are discussed.

notes.statement: Morel et al. (1994) used interval mapping in a backcross of the lupus-susceptible inbred strain NZM/Aeg2410 with C57BL/6 to analyze susceptibility to glomerulonephritis and anti-dsDNA autoantibody production. They identified 3 chromosomal intervals containing strong recessive glomerulonephritis susceptibility alleles on mouse chromosomes 1, 4, and 7.
quotes: The mode of inheritance and the number and location of systemic lupus erythematosus-associated susceptibility loci were analyzed by interval mapping in a backcross with C57BL/6.
Three chromosomal intervals containing strong recessive GN susceptibility alleles were identified on chromosomes 1, 4, and 7, each containing several potentially interesting candidate genes.

notes.statement: Morel et al. (1994) found that heterozygosity at H-2 correlated strongly with glomerulonephritis susceptibility in the NZM/Aeg2410 x C57BL/6 backcross. Logistic regression indicated that each susceptibility allele independently accounted for a component of susceptibility, which was inherited as a threshold genetic liability.
quotes: Heterozygosity at H-2 was also found to correlate strongly with GN susceptibility, consistent with previous findings in the NZB/NZW parental strain model.

Logistic regression analysis indicated that each of these susceptibility alleles independently accounted for a component of GN susceptibility, and that susceptibility was inherited as a threshold genetic liability in this model system.

notes.statement: Weinberg et al. (1980) studied a large pedigree in which 180 relatives were tested. A biological false-positive serologic test for syphilis (BFPSTS) appeared to be inherited as a dominant trait, but the likelihood analysis was inconclusive. No linkage was found between BFPSTS and any blood group or enzyme marker.
quotes: BFPSTS appears dominant, but the analysis was inconclusive. No linkages were found between any disease gene and any marker gene.

notes.statement: Weinberg et al. (1980) found that 2 female members of the pedigree with BFPSTS developed SLE, which agrees with the previously described association. The analysis did not lead to any conclusions about the causal relationship between the 2 traits.
quotes: Two female pedigree members with BFPSTS developed systemic lupus erythematosus, a finding in agreement with the previously described association. The analysis did not lead to any conclusions about the causal relationship between the two traits.

notes.statement: Exner et al. (1980) found the lupus anticoagulant in two pairs of siblings and had strong evidence for it in a third sibling pair. They concluded that the lupus anticoagulant might often be an acquired coagulation defect that requires a genetic predisposition.
quotes: A lupus anticoagulant was detected in plasma from two pairs of siblings using the kaolin clotting time mixing test.
it is apparent that the lupus anticoagulant might often be an acquired coagulation defect requiring genetic predisposition.

notes.statement: Reidenberg et al. (1980) combined their 50 patients with published studies of acetylator phenotype in idiopathic SLE. Worldwide, they found 150 slow and 77 rapid acetylators, compared with the expected 122:105 (P < 0.001). This suggested that slow acetylators were overrepresented among patients with idiopathic SLE.
quotes: These cases plus published studies of acetylator phenotypes in idiopathic SLE show a worldwide distribution of 150 slow to 77 rapid instead of the expected 122:105 (P less than 0.001).

notes.statement: Tan et al. (1982) revised the 1971 preliminary criteria for the classification of SLE to incorporate immunologic knowledge, adding fluorescence antinuclear antibody and antibodies to native DNA and Sm antigen, and aggregating some criteria involving the same organ systems. Raynaud phenomenon and alopecia were dropped because of low sensitivity and specificity.
quotes: The 1982 revised criteria include fluorescence antinuclear antibody and antibody to native DNA and Sm antigen. Some criteria involving the same organ systems were aggregated into single criteria.
Raynaud's phenomenon and alopecia were not included in the 1982 revised criteria because of low sensitivity and specificity.

notes.statement: Tan et al. (1982) found that the revised criteria were 96% sensitive and 96% specific when tested with SLE and control patient data from 18 clinics. They performed better on both measures than the 1971 criteria.
quotes: The new criteria were 96% sensitive and 96% specific when tested with SLE and control patient data gathered from 18 participating clinics.
When compared with the 1971 criteria, the 1982 revised criteria showed gains in sensitivity and specificity.

notes.statement: Lahita et al. (1983) described several families in which SLE occurred mainly in males, chiefly in sons and their fathers. They suggested that in these families the sons inherited the disease from their fathers.
quotes: The disease primarily manifested itself in the sons and in the male parents.
It is suggested that the sons inherited the disease from their fathers in these families.

notes.statement: Lahita et al. (1983) noted that the disease in their male patients with familial SLE was somewhat similar to the disease in BXSB mice.
quotes: The disease in the patients had some similarity to the disease in BXSB mice.

notes.statement: Reveille et al. (1983) studied 8 families, each with 2 or more members with SLE (22 patients in total). Of the 40 relatives without SLE, 7 (18%) had other immune diseases, including thyroid disease, rheumatoid arthritis, ITP, and Henoch-Schonlein purpura. Eleven of these relatives (28%) had ANA and 11 (28%) had antibodies to ssDNA.
quotes: Among the 40 non-SLE relatives, 7 (18%) had other immune diseases, including thyroid disease in 2, rheumatoid arthritis in 2, ITP in 2, and Henoch-Schönlein purpura in one.
Eleven non-SLE relatives (28%) had ANA, which was in high-titer in 5 (13%). Eleven (28%) had antibodies to ssDNA, and one had a BFP.

notes.statement: Reveille et al. (1983) found that HLA-DR2 and DR3 each occurred in 36% of familial SLE patients, which did not differ significantly from relatives or controls. Sib pair analysis of 14 sets, 7 of them from published reports, showed only a random distribution of HLA haplotypes with SLE. The authors concluded that genetic factors other than HLA and complement component deficiencies, and/or environmental factors, are necessary for SLE to be expressed.
quotes: HLA-DR2 occurred in 36% and DR3 in 36% of SLE patients, which was not significantly different from either non-SLE family members or unrelated local controls.
Sib pair analysis of seven sets presented here and seven from two published reports, demonstrated only random distribution with SLE.
These data strongly suggest that genetic factors (other than HLA and complement component deficiencies) and/or environmental factors are necessary for the expression of SLE

notes.statement: Reveille et al. (1983) found DR2 and/or DR3 in 5 of 6 familial SLE patients (83%) with anti-Ro(SSA) antibodies, but the difference was not significant.
quotes: Interestingly, DR2 and/or DR3 were found in five of the six patients (83%) having anti-ro(SSA) antibodies (p = NS).

notes.statement: Diamond and Scharff (1984) found that U4, a somatic mutant of the S107 antiphosphocholine (T15 idiotype) myeloma line, had a single glutamic acid-to-alanine substitution at residue 35 of the heavy chain. This change caused loss of phosphocholine binding and gain of reactivity with double-stranded DNA, protamine, and cardiolipin. They concluded that a single amino acid change could transform an antibacterial antibody into one resembling the autoantibodies seen in autoimmune disease in mice and man.
quotes: A somatic mutant of this line, U4, makes an immunoglobulin with a single amino acid substitution of an alanine for a glutamic acid at residue 35. This single amino acid change results in a loss of phosphocholine binding activity.
However, the U4 immunoglobulin has acquired reactivity with a variety of phosphorylated macromolecules, including double-stranded DNA, protamine, and cardiolipin.
Thus, a single amino acid change in the T15 heavy chain can transform an antibacterial antibody into an antibody that resembles the autoantibodies seen in mice and man with autoimmune disease.

notes.statement: Fielder et al. (1983) studied the families of 29 patients with SLE and 42 normal subjects. Null (silent) alleles for C4A, C4B, or C2 were found in 24 of the 29 patients (83%) and in 18 of the 42 controls (43%). HLA-DR3 was present in 20 of the patients (69%) and 7 of 39 controls (18%).
quotes: Null (silent) alleles for C4A, C4B, or C2 were found in 24 of the 29 (83%) patients compared with 18 of the 42 (43%) normal controls.
HLA-DR3 was present in 20 (69%) of the patients and seven out of 39 (18%) of the normal controls.

notes.statement: Fielder et al. (1983) found strong linkage disequilibrium between DR3 and the C4A and C4B null alleles, and their data could not separate the relative contributions of DR3 and the C4 null alleles as genetic risk factors. They suggested that, because SLE is known to be associated with complement deficiencies, the C4A, C4B and C2 null alleles found in most patients are relevant to susceptibility.
quotes: There was strong linkage disequilibrium between DR3 and the null alleles for C4A and C4B. The data did not permit the relative contributions of DR3 and null factors of C4A and C4B as genetic risk factors to be distinguished.
suggests, however, that the presence of null alleles for C4A and C4B, as well as C2, found in most of the patients, is relevant to their genetic susceptibility to this disease.

notes.statement: Steinberg et al. (1984) reviewed murine models of SLE. They noted that most autoantibody-producing B cells could be eliminated from mice with lupus by the presence of the xid gene. They also noted that giving an arachidonic acid analog was an effective treatment for murine lupus.
quotes: Most autoantibody-producing B cells can be eliminated from mice with lupus erythematosus by virtue of the presence of the gene, xid.
administration of an analog of arachidonic acid is an effective treatment for murine lupus erythematosus.

notes.statement: Steinberg et al. (1984) proposed that genetic factors predispose to SLE. In their view, some genes may produce a generalized immune abnormality and others may lead to specific autoantibodies, while environmental triggers such as bacterial and viral infections increase autoantibody production by activating macrophages and T cells, which in turn stimulate B cells.
quotes: Genetic factors appear to play an important predisposing role in the disorder: The presence of certain genes may produce a generalized immune abnormality, whereas others may lead to specific autoantibodies.
Bacterial and viral illnesses can provide stimulation by activating macrophages and T cells that, in turn, stimulate B cells.

notes.statement: Solomon et al. (1983) purified anti-native DNA antibodies from a patient with active SLE and raised mouse monoclonal anti-idiotypic antibodies against them. One of these, 3I, recognized an idiotype outside the antigen-binding site. 3I reacted with 8 of 9 sera that had anti-native DNA activity, which suggested that anti-native DNA antibodies from unrelated SLE patients share a common idiotype.
quotes: Antinative DNA antibodies were purified from the serum of a patient with active systemic lupus erythematosus. Using hybridoma technology, we produced several mouse monoclonal antibodies directed against idiotypic determinants on these antinative DNA antibodies.
Eight of nine sera containing antinative DNA activity as determined by the Millipore filter assay reacted with 3I in a solid-phase radioimmunoassay.
These findings suggest that antinative DNA antibodies from nonrelated patients with systemic lupus erythematosus share a common idiotype.

notes.statement: Batchelor et al. (1980) found HLA-DR4 in 73% of 26 patients with hydralazine-induced SLE. This was significantly higher than in 113 healthy controls (33%), 16 slow-acetylator hypertensive patients who took hydralazine for more than a year without developing SLE (25%), and 20 patients with idiopathic SLE (25%).
quotes: The frequency of HLA-DR4 (73%) was significantly higher in the group with hydralazine-induced SLE than in the other groups (respectively 33%, 25%, and 25%).

notes.statement: Batchelor et al. (1980) found that among slow acetylators treated with hydralazine, every woman with DR4 developed hydralazine-induced SLE. The only men who developed it carried DR2 and were taking 200 mg of hydralazine per day. Women outnumbered men 4:1.
quotes: If the slow acetylators treated with hydralazine were analysed as one group, it was observed that all women with DR4 developed hydralazine-induced SLE; the only men to do so were those with DR2 who were receiving 200 mg hydralazine per day.

notes.statement: Batchelor et al. (1980) found that the distribution of DR antigens in hydralazine-induced SLE differed significantly from that in idiopathic SLE. They took this as support for the view that the two syndromes are separate entities.
quotes: It was also noted that the distribution of DR antigens in the hydralazine-SLE patients was significantly different from that in the group with idiopathic SLE. This supports the view that the syndromes are separate entities.

notes.statement: Batchelor et al. (1980) suggested guidelines for hydralazine therapy based on HLA-DR type and sex.
quotes: These observations have led us to suggest guide lines for hydralazine therapy and point to a striking association between an HLA-DR antigen and an adverse reaction to a therapeutic agent.

notes.statement: Siegel et al. (1970) reported epidemiologic studies of systemic lupus erythematosus that compared data for New York City and Jefferson County, Alabama, over 1956 to 1965.
quotes: Epidemiologic studies on systemic lupus erythematosus. Comparative data for New York City and Jefferson County, Alabama, 1956-1965.

notes.statement: As part of a series of family studies in systemic lupus erythematosus, Larsen and Godal (1972) studied thyroid diseases and thyroid antibodies in SLE families.
quotes: Family studies in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). IX. Thyroid diseases and antibodies.

notes.statement: First (1973) reported familial occurrence of systemic lupus erythematosus.
quotes: Familial systemic lupus erythematosus.

notes.statement: Reed et al. (1972) described hereditary inflammatory vasculitis with persistent nodules as a genetically determined new entity that they considered probably related to lupus erythematosus.
quotes: Hereditary inflammatory vasculitis with persistent nodules. A genetically-determined new entity probably related to lupus erythematosus.

notes.statement: In a community-based study of systemic lupus erythematosus, Fessel (1974) examined incidence, prevalence, outcome, and first symptoms, and found a high prevalence of the disorder in black women.
quotes: Systemic lupus erythematosus in the community. Incidence, prevalence, outcome, and first symptoms; the high prevalence in black women.

notes.statement: Lappat and Cawein (1968) reported a familial study of procainamide-induced systemic lupus erythematosus. They raised the question of whether a pharmacogenetic polymorphism was involved.
quotes: A familial study of procainamide-induced systemic lupus erythematosus. A question of pharmacogenetic polymorphism.

notes.statement: Larsen (1972) carried out family studies in systemic lupus erythematosus, starting from a series of probands from central eastern Norway.
quotes: Family studies in systemic lupus erythematosus. I. A proband material from central eastern Norway.

notes.statement: Tuffanelli (1971) described lupus erythematosus panniculitis (lupus profundus), a form of lupus erythematosus that affects the subcutaneous fat.
quotes: Lupus erythematosus panniculitis (profundus).

notes.statement: Theofilopoulos and Dixon (1985) reviewed murine models of systemic lupus erythematosus.
quotes: Murine models of systemic lupus erythematosus.

notes.statement: Halpern et al. (1985) studied 3 kindreds with familial SLE. They found a cross-reactive idiotype (3I) found on anti-DNA antibodies at high titer in 15 of 19 family members without SLE, while only 2 of these relatives had anti-DNA antibodies. They concluded that expression of the idiotype was significantly increased in relatives of SLE patients and usually occurred without anti-DNA activity.
quotes: serum samples from 6 of 8 SLE patients and 15 of 19 family members had high-titered reactivity with the antiidiotype, 3I
This study indicates that expression of an idiotype associated with anti-DNA antibodies is significantly increased in relatives of SLE patients and usually occurs in the absence of anti-DNA activity.

notes.statement: Halpern et al. (1985) found that cationic 3I-reactive immunoglobulin bands (pH 7-8.5) correlated with the presence of anti-DNA antibodies. They suggested that immunoglobulin charge may help determine specificity for DNA. In 2 additional SLE patients and 2 additional relatives, anti-DNA antibodies were detected only under conditions that dissociate immune complexes.
quotes: Cationic bands were found to correlate with the presence of anti-DNA antibodies, indicating that immunoglobulin charge may be a factor in determining specificity for DNA.
In 2 additional SLE patients and 2 additional family members, anti-DNA antibodies were revealed when sera were analyzed under conditions that dissociate immune complexes.

notes.statement: Fronek et al. (1986) examined restriction fragment length polymorphisms of the T cell receptor beta chain genes and found a similar distribution in SLE patients, their relatives, and normal controls. They suggested that these genes are not coinherited with genes responsible for SLE.
quotes: The restriction fragment length polymorphism distribution was similar in systemic lupus erythematosus patients, their relatives, and normal controls.
Our observations suggest that these genes are not coinherited with genes responsible for systemic lupus erythematosus.

notes.statement: Baer et al. (1986) found that the slow acetylator phenotype was about as frequent in 64 patients with idiopathic SLE (38%) as in 60 healthy volunteers (50%) and 52 non-SLE medical service patients (44%). It was also not more frequent in SLE subgroups defined by demographic features or by specific disease manifestations. The authors concluded that there was no evidence for an association between acetylator phenotype and idiopathic SLE.
quotes: the frequency of the slow acetylator phenotype was similar in 64 patients with idiopathic SLE (38%), 60 healthy volunteers (50%), and 52 non-SLE medical service patients (44%)
The slow acetylator phenotype was not more frequent among subgroups of the SLE patients defined by demographic features or specific manifestations of disease.
do not provide evidence for an association between acetylator phenotype and idiopathic SLE

notes.statement: Mackie et al. (1987) found prolonged, non-correctable KPTTs in 4 healthy spouses of affected females and in 3 asymptomatic sibs in 3 families with SLE or lupus-like disease. They concluded that these findings supported a hypothesis that transmissible agents or other environmental factors are involved in lupus-like disorders.
quotes: Four healthy spouses of affected females, and three asymptomatic siblings also had prolonged non-correctable KPTTs.
These findings would support a hypothesis of transmissible agents or other environmental factors being involved in lupus-like disorders.

notes.statement: Mackie et al. (1987) found that anticardiolipin levels were raised in subjects with lupus anticoagulant. However, length of the KPTT did not correlate closely with anticardiolipin titer.
quotes: Although anticardiolipin levels are raised in subjects with LA, there was no close correlation between length of KPTT and anticardiolipin titre.

notes.statement: Green et al. (1986) used the empirical logistic method to analyze data on the reported associations of HLA-DR3 and null (QO) alleles at the C4A and C4B loci with SLE. The analysis suggested that the association with C4 null alleles is primary and that the DR3 association is likely secondary to it, which may give information on the location of the HLA-linked susceptibility gene.
quotes: The analysis suggests that the association with null alleles at the C4 loci is primary and the DR3 association is likely to be secondary to this.
The empirical logistic method has been applied to a body of data which included the relevant genotypes.

notes.statement: Levcovitz et al. (1988) found that PHA-stimulated lymphocytes from all patients with SLE produced two classes of newly synthesized DNA on sucrose density gradients. One was a large-molecular-weight fraction that ran with control DNA. The other was an excess low-molecular-weight DNA fraction that control lymphocytes did not have. The excess LMW-DNA did not depend on disease activity or drug therapy.
quotes: All patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) demonstrated two classes of newly synthesized DNA in sucrose density gradients of PHA (phytohemagglutinin)-stimulated lymphocytes
Excess LMW-DNA was independent of disease activity or drug therapy.

notes.statement: Levcovitz et al. (1988) concluded that excess LMW-DNA in stimulated lymphocytes was inherited as an autosomal dominant trait in a family with SLE in first cousins. The trait occurred in both males and females, and male-to-male transmission was seen.
quotes: Both males and females had excess LMW-DNA. Male-male transmission was observed. The expression of excess LMW-DNA in stimulated lymphocytes is inherited as an autosomal dominant genetic trait in this family.

notes.statement: In this family, Levcovitz et al. (1988) found that every unaffected adult relative with excess LMW-DNA had positive antinuclear antibodies, except the grandmother. None of the 5 children with excess LMW-DNA had positive ANAs. The authors suggested that excess LMW-DNA appears before ANAs and may predispose to the immunologic responses of SLE.
quotes: All unaffected adult family members with the marker had positive antinuclear antibodies (ANAs) except the grandmother. However, none of the five children with excess LMW-DNA showed positive ANAs.

Excess LMW-DNA precedes the appearance of ANAs when found in children of adults with excess LMW-DNA, and may be a predisposing factor in the development of the immunologic responses of systemic lupus erythematosus.

notes.statement: Wong et al. (1988) studied RFLPs of the T cell receptor alpha, beta, and gamma chain genes by Southern blot in 5 families with multiple members with SLE, 14 unrelated SLE patients, and 14 controls. They found no significant difference in RFLP pattern distribution among patients, relatives, and controls, and none of the 3 TcR genes cosegregated with SLE in the multiplex families; they concluded that these genes are not likely to be linked to SLE.
quotes: Polymorphic patterns were detected with probes for all 3 TcR chains, but there was no significant difference in the distribution of the restriction fragment length polymorphism pattern among the patients, the relatives, and the controls.
We conclude that TcR alpha, beta, and gamma chain genes are not likely to be linked to genes related to SLE.

notes.statement: Sakane et al. (1989) studied 34 clinically healthy family members of 6 SLE probands. Impaired phytohemagglutinin-induced IL-2 activity was found in 15 of 29 blood relatives but in none of 5 unrelated household members, suggesting that impaired IL-2 activity correlates strongly with a genetic relationship.
quotes: in 34 clinically healthy family members of six SLE probands
Impaired IL-2 activity was found in 15 of the 29 consanguineous relatives.
none of the five nonconsanguineous household persons had abnormal results

notes.statement: Sakane et al. (1989) found increased spontaneous immunoglobulin-secreting B cells in 22 of 29 blood relatives of SLE probands, and also in 4 of 5 unrelated household members. They concluded that although the evidence favored a genetic basis for the B-cell abnormalities, environmental effects may also contribute to their familial occurrence.
quotes: Results for the B-cell assay were abnormal in 22 of the 29 consanguineous relatives.
four of the five nonconsanguineous household relatives also had abnormal assay results
Although the evidence favors a genetic basis for the B-cell abnormalities, environmental effects may also contribute to the familial occurrence of these abnormalities.

notes.statement: Stohl et al. (1985) found from family studies that the T4 epitope phenotype seemed to be inherited in an autosomal codominant way and was not linked to the HLA locus. The asymptomatic T4 epitope-deficient brother of one patient had lymphadenopathy in the same distribution as his sister with SLE.
quotes: Family studies pointed to an autosomal codominant mode of inheritance not linked to the HLA locus for the T4 epitope phenotype.
The asymptomatic and otherwise healthy T4 epitope-deficient brother of one of these patients also had lymphadenopathy in a distribution identical to that of his sister with SLE.

notes.statement: Stohl et al. (1985) found that, compared with cells from T4 epitope-intermediate relatives, peripheral blood mononuclear cells from T4 epitope-deficient family members showed impaired B-cell differentiation after stimulation with pokeweed mitogen. Helper/suppressor T-cell ratios, autoantibodies, and proliferation in response to mitogens and in mixed lymphocyte reactions did not correlate with T4 epitope phenotype.
quotes: Cultures of peripheral-blood mononuclear cells revealed impaired B-cell differentiation upon stimulation with pokeweed mitogen in cells originating from the T4 epitope-deficient family members as compared with those originating from their T4 epitope-intermediate relatives.

Ratios of T helper/inducer cells to T suppressor/cytotoxic cells, the presence of various autoantibodies, and proliferation in response to mitogens and in the mixed lymphocyte reactions did not correlate with T4 epitope phenotype.

notes.statement: Stohl et al. (1985) suggested that SLE with the T4 epitope-deficient phenotype may be a distinct subset of SLE with its own clinical and immunologic properties.
quotes: We suggest that SLE in association with the T4 epitope-deficient phenotype may represent a unique subset of patients with SLE that has distinct clinical and immunologic properties.

notes.statement: Sturfelt et al. (1990) found homozygous C4A deficiency in 13 of 80 (16%) patients with SLE, representing all diagnosed cases from a defined population in southern Sweden, minimizing patient selection bias.
quotes: Homozygous C4A deficiency was found at a prevalence of 16% (13/80 patients) in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).
The patients represented all diagnosed cases retrieved from a defined population in Southern Sweden, which minimizes the influence of patient selection.

notes.statement: Sturfelt et al. (1990) found that photosensitivity was more common in C4A-deficient SLE patients than in other SLE patients (p less than 0.05), resembling findings in complete classical pathway deficiencies; other clinical features and autoantibody profiles (anti-dsDNA, anti-Sm, anti-RNP, anti-SSA, anti-SSB, rheumatoid factors, anticardiolipin) did not differ.
quotes: Photosensitivity was more common among C4A-deficient patients than among other SLE patients (p less than 0.05). Otherwise, clinical features were similar in the two groups.
no differences were found with regard to presence of various autoantibodies (anti-dsDNA, anti-Sm, anti-RNP, anti-SSA, anti-SSB, rheumatoid factors and anti-cardiolipin)
The increased photosensitivity of C4A-deficient patients partly resembles the findings in patients with complete deficiencies of classical pathway components.

notes.statement: Sturfelt et al. (1990) found that in SLE patients expressing both C4A and C4B isotypes, plasma C4B/C4A quotients were fairly stable irrespective of disease activity, arguing against preferential breakdown of either isotype during complement activation.
quotes: In patients expressing both C4A and C4B isotypes, C4B/C4A quotients were fairly stable in plasma irrespective of disease activity. This argues against preferential break-down of either isotype during complement activation in the disease.

notes.statement: Block et al. (1975) studied 12 twin pairs with SLE. Four of 7 definitely monozygotic pairs (57%) were concordant for clinical SLE, and all 3 dizygotic pairs were discordant. In the monozygotic pairs, concordance for antinuclear factor was 71% and for hypergammaglobulinemia 87%. These figures agreed closely with 12 previously described monozygotic sets.
quotes: In the present series, four of seven (57 per cent) definitely monozygotic pairs were clinically concordant for SLE

Concordance for the presence of antinuclear factor (ANF) and hypergammaglobulinemia was 71 and tinuclear factor (ANF) and hypergammaglobulinemia was 71 and 87 per cent, respiectively. These data closely agree with those on the 12 definitely monozygotic sets previously described.

notes.statement: Block et al. (1975) compared their twin data with data from other first-degree relatives of the twins. They concluded that the comparison clearly suggested a strong genetic component in the pathogenesis of SLE, and that nongenetic and environmental factors also contributed to expression of the disease.
quotes: Comparison of these data with thos from other first degree relatives of out twins clearly suggests a strong genetic component in the pathogenesis of SLE. The relative contribution of nongenetic and environmental factors to the expression of the disease is discussed.

notes.statement: DeHoratius et al. (1975) found anti-RNA antibodies in 16% of 124 family members of SLE probands, compared with 5% of 76 control family members. Among the SLE family members, these antibodies occurred only in close household contacts of the probands (21% of 94). They were present in consanguineous household contacts but not in nonconsanguineous ones.
quotes: Anti-RNA antibodies were found in 82% of 28 systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) probands and in 16% of 124 of their family members. The incidence in 76 control family members was only 5%.
In the SLE family members, the antibodies were found exclusively in 21% of the 94 close household contacts of the probands.
The anti-RNA antibodies were present in consanguineous household contacts but not in nonconsanguineous household contacts.

notes.statement: DeHoratius et al. (1975) found anti-native DNA antibodies in 6% of close household contacts of SLE probands, which did not differ significantly from the 1% found in control families. Lymphocytotoxic antibodies were found in 57% of SLE family members overall and in 68% of close household contacts.
quotes: The incidence of anti-nDNA antibodies in close household contacts of the probands was 6%, which was not significantly different from the 1% incidence found in control families.
Lymphocytotoxic antibodies occurred in 57% of the SLE family members as a whole and in 68% of the close household contacts.

notes.statement: DeHoratius et al. (1975) found that, in SLE probands, lymphocytotoxic antibodies correlated with anti-poly A and anti-native DNA antibodies but not with anti-poly A-poly U. In household contacts, lymphocytotoxic antibodies correlated with anti-poly A-poly U but not with anti-poly A or anti-native DNA. The authors concluded that the findings strengthened the hypothesis that both an environmental agent, possibly a virus, and the genetic response are important in the pathogenesis of SLE.
quotes: In the SLE probands, lymphocytotoxic antibodies correlated with anti-single-stranded RNA (poly A) and anti-nDNA but not with anti-double-stranded RNA (poly A-poly U).
These findings strengthen the hypothesis that both an environmental agent, possibly a virus, as well as the genetic response are important in the pathogenesis of SLE.

notes.statement: Arnett and Shulman (1976) studied 8 families with familial SLE. Together with 1 deceased pair and 31 families from the literature, the families included 8 pairs of identical twins, 1 pair of non-identical twins, 16 sib combinations and 15 parent-offspring combinations. They found marked concordance for how the disease presented between identical twins and between parents and offspring, but not between sibs. They concluded that these findings supported genetic influences on SLE.
quotes: These families, plus one deceased pair and 31 described in the literature consisted of 8 pairs of identical twins, one pair of non-identical twins, and 16 sibling and 15 parent-offspring combinations.
Impressive concordance for disease expression was found between pairs of identical twins and between parent and offspring. No such concordance was found between siblings and controls.

notes.statement: Arnett and Shulman (1976) found 4 father-offspring pairs. They said this made it less likely that SLE is passed on around the time of birth.
quotes: The finding of four father-offspring pairs lessens the possibility that SLE is transmitted during the perinatal period.

notes.statement: Arnett and Shulman (1976) found that identical twins developed SLE within an average of 2 years of each other. In sibs, the average difference in age at onset was 9 years, but the average gap in calendar date of onset was only 3 years. For parents and offspring, the corresponding figures were 20 and 8 years. The authors suggested this pointed to environmental influences in starting SLE, especially in sibs.
quotes: The onset of SLE in each of identical twins occurred within an average of 2 years. In siblings, however, while the average difference in age at onset was 9 years, the average difference in time of onset (actual date) was only 3 years.
Comparable figures for parents and offspring were 20 and 8 years, respectively. These data suggest environmental influences in the initiation of SLE, especially in siblings.

notes.statement: Arnett and Shulman (1976) compared familial SLE cases with matched non-familial controls on 23 clinical and laboratory features and found no real differences. They concluded that familial SLE is probably not a separate disease from non-familial SLE.
quotes: Comparison of the frequencies of clinical and laboratory attributes in the familial group as opposed to non-familial groups showed no real differences. Thus, familial SLE is probably not a different disease entity from non-familial SLE.

notes.statement: Arnett and Shulman (1976) examined 27 unaffected first-degree relatives. Two sisters had thyroid disease, persistent leukopenia and a raised sedimentation rate; their mother had SLE and Hashimoto thyroiditis and their sib had SLE. The other 25 relatives were clinically, hematologically, biochemically and serologically normal.
quotes: Studies of 27 unaffected first-degree relatives in our eight families revealed two sisters with thyroid disease, persistent leukopenia and sedimentation rate elevation.
The remaining 25 relatives were clinically, hematologically, biochemically, and serologically normal.

notes.statement: Knight and Adams (1978) studied the incidence of early severe lupus nephritis, identified by antemortem renal function tests, in 230 (NZB x NZW) x NZW and 150 (NZB x NZW) x NZB backcross mice. The data indicated that the NZB strain contributed only 1 gene and the NZW strain contributed 2 genes, or clusters of closely linked genes, to the renal disorder of the F1 hybrid; 1 of the NZW genes was linked to the H-2 complex.
quotes: we have studied the incidence of the renal disease in 230 (NZB x NZW) x NZW backcross mice (an earlier study) and, in this study, in 150 (NZB x NZW) x NZB backcross mice.

The data indicate that the NZB strain contributes only one gene and the NZW strain contributes two genes, or clusters of closely linked genes, to the renal disorder of the F1 hybrid. One of the NZW genes was found to be linked to the H-2 complex.

notes.statement: Knight and Adams (1978) concluded that all 3 genes must be dominant or codominant, because their effect was expressed in the heterozygous state, and noted that neither inbred parental strain showed the disorder.
quotes: All three genes must be dominant or codominant, as their effect is expressed in the heterozygous state.
as neither of the inbred parental strains shows the disorder

notes.statement: In a survey of civilian general hospitals on Oahu, Hawaii, for 1970-1975, Serdula and Rhoads (1979) found 168 cases of SLE, 107 of them definite. Age-adjusted prevalence rates per 100,000 for definite cases at the end of 1975 were 5.8 in whites, 24.1 in Chinese, 19.9 in Filipinos, 20.4 in part-Hawaiians, and 18.2 in Japanese.
quotes: One hundred sixty-eight cases were ascertained, of which 107 were considered "definite."
Age-adjusted prevalence rates per 100,000 were estimated for definite cases at the end of 1975 as follows: white 5.8, Chinese 24.1, Filipino 19.9, part-Hawaiian 20.4, and Japanese 18.2.

notes.statement: Serdula and Rhoads (1979) found a strong female preponderance in every ethnic group, with females making up an average of 90% of definite cases overall.
quotes: There was a heavy preponderance of females in each ethnic group, averaging 90% of the definite cases overall.

notes.statement: Serdula and Rhoads (1979) reported age-adjusted SLE mortality rates per million of 3.04 for US whites, 8.82 for US nonwhites, 1.89 for Hawaii whites, and 14.46 for Hawaii nonwhites. They stated that the cause of the very high SLE prevalence and mortality in the Oriental and Polynesian people of Hawaii was not clear.
quotes: Review of vital statistics for the United States and Hawaii during this period showed age-adjusted SLE mortality rates per million as follows: U.S. white 3.04, U.S. non-white 8.82, Hawaii white 1.89, Hawaii non-white 14.46.
The cause of the very high SLE prevalence and mortality in the Oriental and Polynesian people of Hawaii is not clear.

notes.statement: Miller and Schwartz (1979) used an in vitro suppressor-cell assay to study 15 SLE patients, 50 of their clinically healthy family members and 41 normal persons. They found abnormal suppressor-cell activity in 13 first-degree relatives, 12 of whom were women. The results did not correlate with the presence of lymphocytotoxic antibodies in the relatives.
quotes: Abnormal suppressor-cell activity was also found in 13 first-degree relatives, 12 of whom were women.
We found no correlation between results of the suppressor-cell assay and the presence or absence of lymphocytotoxic antibodies in the relatives.

notes.statement: Miller and Schwartz (1979) concluded that impaired suppressor-cell function cannot by itself explain the pathogenesis of SLE but that certain suppressor-cell abnormalities are genetic markers. They proposed that SLE develops only when at least two functionally distinct classes of genes are involved.
quotes: Impaired suppressor-cell function cannot by itself explain the pathogenesis of systemic lupus erythematosus. Our results support the hypothesis that certain abnormalities of suppressor cells are genetic markers.
We propose that the development of systemic lupus erythematosus requires the participation of at least two functionally distinct classes of genes.

notes.statement: Horn et al. (1978) studied 18 additional family members across three generations of a kindred in which a brother and sister had mixed connective tissue disease. They found symptoms or signs of MCTD, without full expression of the disease, in 8 relatives. Rheumatoid factor was positive in 9 of 17 relatives, at titers of 1:160 to 1:2560.
quotes: Symptoms or signs of MCTD without complete expression of the disease were found in 8 relatives of the original cases.
Tests for rheumatoid factor were positive in 9 of 17 relatives of the patients; the titers ranged from 1:160 to 1:2560.

notes.statement: Horn et al. (1978) found that the 2 sibs with MCTD had an identical HLA genotype (11,12/2,12). Three other sibs with impressive rheumatic complaints also inherited this genotype. The authors emphasized an association between inflammatory connective tissue disease and a specific HLA type within a single kindred.
quotes: The brother and sister with MCTD had an identical HLA genotype--11,12/2,12. The same genotype was inherited by 3 of their siblings, who had impressive rheumatic complaints.
This report emphasizes the association between inflammatory connective tissue disease and a specific HLA type within a single kindred.

notes.statement: Beaucher et al. (1977) reported familial lupus erythematosus in which antibodies to DNA were found in the household dogs.
quotes: Familial lupus erythematosus. Antibodies to DNA in household dogs.

notes.statement: Yocum et al. (1975) studied a pair of monozygotic twins discordant for SLE. Both twins had biologically false-positive serology at an early age, but only one developed SLE; the twins showed no differences in immune responses to tetanus toxoid, keyhole limpet hemocyanin, DNCB, delayed sensitivity, or antiviral antibody titers.
quotes: A pair of monozygotic twins discordant for systemic lupus erythematosus(SLE) were studied and no differences noted in their immune respose to tetanus toxoid, keyhole lympet hemocyanin, DNCB, delayed sensitivity, or antibody titers to viruses.
Both were noted to have biologically false positive serology at an early age, but only one twon developed SLE.

notes.statement: Yocum et al. (1975) noted that the clinically unaffected twin of a monozygotic pair discordant for SLE had undergone castration at an early age, suggesting that ovarian hormones may play an important role in the development of SLE.
quotes: The clinically unaffected twin underwent castration at an early age, suggesting that ovarian hormones may play an important role in the development of SLE.
